Photo taken with a mobile phone on July 6, 2026 in the Wadi Halfa area of northern Sudan after a gold mine collapse. Photo by Mohamed Osman/Xinhua via Getty Images.
_Story by Aunnab Alman_
WEST KORDOFAN, Sudan--At 3 p.m. on Tuesday, September 15, Abu Fayza al-Fadil, 32, climbed out of one of six interconnected shafts at Sudan's Al-Zaraa gold mine to take a break.
Minutes later, the shafts collapsed, burying dozens of his colleagues underground.
"I went out to rest for a few minutes, and suddenly the ground shook and the shaft disappeared, along with everyone inside it," al-Fadil told Drop Site by phone from a Starlink point in the village of Al-Raqeeq, where the mine is located.
"There were just a few minutes between me and death," he said. At the time, he had been thinking about his wife and their two young children.
Around 45 men had been working in the shaft he had just left, al-Fadil said. Yet, paramilitary fighters stationed nearby refused to help, survivors say.
Mohammed al-Hassan was in a second shaft when it gave way. "There were about 60 of us down there when it collapsed," he told Drop Site.

"Twenty-five died. We pulled their bodies out ourselves. Seventeen of us made it, six of them injured, and we got them out with our own hands. The others are still missing. We don't know what happened to them."
Al-Hassan said the miners asked the RSF for help and were turned away. "We went to a Rapid Support Forces post about 15 minutes away and told them people were trapped," he said. "They had two excavators, and they refused to help."
All six shafts collapsed into one another, burying the miners inside. At least 82 people were killed and around 50 injured, a local administration official [told reporters](https://substack.com/redirect/d92eb07a-af57-4eb5-8267-ff4f42c6699b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the following day. A source in the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the paramilitary group that controls the area, gave AFP [the same death toll](https://substack.com/redirect/101e631d-9739-4bba-98bb-db3c1c2f792c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and said an unknown number of people remained trapped.
No updated toll has been released since. A few days after the collapse, the RSF sealed off the area around the mine, local sources said, clearing out even the miners who were searching for their colleagues. No one has been allowed near the mine since.
The RSF was itself a partner in running the mine, according to local miners, after they took control of West Kordofan state in December 2025. Gold is one of the main sources of revenue for both sides of Sudan's war--the national military, the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), and the RSF--according to conflict economy experts. Over two million people work in the mining industry in Sudan.
But the sector remains dangerously unregulated. This is the fourth major gold mine collapse in Sudan this year, following Abu Jubeiha in January, where at least six miners died, Keliti in April, which killed at least seven, and Wadi Halfa in July, where 15 died.
Occupational safety experts say the pattern is the same each time. Informal shafts are dug without oversight. The Al-Zaraa mine, near the town of Al-Nuhud, was made up of deep, interconnected pits dug without safety equipment or shoring, the temporary supports that hold up a shaft's walls and roof. Local residents dug them in recent years.

Rescue fell to local residents. Al-Tahir Issa, 30, lives in Al-Raqeeq and arrived within an hour of the collapse.
"We found the young men in a state of shock and bewilderment. Some of them did not know what had happened, while others had managed to get out on their own, some with injuries and fractures," said Issa.
"We locals volunteered to help. We brought our tools from home like pickaxes and shovels, and began trying to rescue those trapped and give first aid to those coming out of the mine."
"By the second day, we had recovered 25 bodies and 13 injured people," said Issa, describing the recovery effort he joined. "After the bodies were recovered, we performed the funeral prayer for them."
There is no conventional mobile network or public internet in the area. Survivors and residents could speak to Drop Site only intermittently, from shops and spaces with Starlink terminals, which are also under RSF control. Many were hesitant to discuss the mine or the authorities who run it.
None of the miners Drop Site spoke to saw medical teams or any response from the authorities, whether the RSF's civil administration or the national government. The Sudanese Mineral Resources Company, the state body that oversees mining, has not issued any statement on the Al-Zaraa collapse, although it did comment days later on a collapse at the Awni mine in Red Sea State.
Among the dead was Abu Bakr Hamid al-Daqil, 27, who was in a third shaft with around 30 other workers. None of them survived. Since his father's death, he had been the sole provider for his mother, Halima Mustafa, and his sister, Fatima.
"When we heard about the collapse, we waited to find out whether Abu Bakr had made it out," his mother said.
Mohammed al-Zaki, 26, also died in the collapse. His sister, Lamia, said he had been studying economics at Bahri University in Khartoum North when the war broke out and classes were suspended.
"He decided he did not want to continue his studies and would go to work in the mines. He knew the work was hard, but he went because he wanted to establish himself and get married," she said. "After a year of working in various mines, he died, leaving grief in our hearts that will never heal."
Khaled Qarashi, a researcher and environmental activist with the [Sudanese Environmental Conservation Society](https://substack.com/redirect/554d9168-b77d-401f-acab-7faf61a5a138?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), said most miners have no knowledge of soil conditions.
"Informal mining relies on shallow digging without any shoring, personal protective equipment or rescue tools," he said. "The authorities only take notice after major disasters have occurred, at which point they intervene to close the mines temporarily, only to reopen them later."
**Lack of Opportunities**
Mohammed Haroun, who manages a mining pit in Northern State where the SAF is in control, said young men have few alternatives. "Rampant unemployment, deteriorating living conditions and a lack of opportunities, even before the war, coupled with the war's worsening of these conditions, have made mining the only viable option for them to provide for their families," he said.
Pits are owned by individuals or investors who pay for the digging and basic tools, Haroun said. Workers are paid through a quota system based on daily output. "Once the gold has been extracted, local traders and collectors buy it for cash, and it is then transported through commercial networks to the major markets."
There is no set income, Haroun said. A miner who goes down the shafts might spend three months at a mine and find a single piece of gold worth around $2,000, or earn nothing at all. Workers at the washing mills, where material from the shafts is washed until the gold separates out, are paid by the load. Washing one sack can bring in the equivalent of about $30, though rates vary from well to well and mine to mine.
Gold was a source of rivalry between the SAF and the RSF even before the war began in April 2023. As the fighting continued, the country's gold fields were effectively divided between the two sides.
According to London-based think tank [Chatham House](https://substack.com/redirect/d21b081c-fbff-4249-a0ab-aadec02f1127?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the army controls the main mining areas in River Nile, Northern, Red Sea and South Kordofan states, while the RSF oversees mining in Darfur and parts of Kordofan, including West Kordofan.
In RSF areas, Chatham House found, the paramilitaries protect mining and related trade, impose set channels for selling gold, and, in some cases, take part in production directly. In army-held areas, production and trade run through institutions linked to the government in Port Sudan, while cross-border smuggling has grown.
Profits from gold, the study found, pay for weapons and goods that help both sides and their allies keep fighting. Large quantities of gold have been [smuggled out of the country to finance the RSF](https://substack.com/redirect/3556d1f2-2fd3-4b94-a8db-5507fe334419?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), according to experts commissioned by the United Nations.
Less than a week after Al-Zaraa, a fifth mine collapsed, this time at Awny in Red Sea State, near the Egyptian border, [killing at least 10 people](https://substack.com/redirect/e29df4dd-ab9e-4b70-8880-8e1d138ce4a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and injuring 21, according to survivors. Unlike Al-Zaraa, Awny lies in army-held territory, as do the Keliti and Wadi Halfa mines that collapsed earlier this year.

body:
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Gina here, Peter. I just got off the phone with our Field Director.
We went over our campaign’s get-out-the-vote plan for these final 30 days until Election Day — and since you’ve been a dedicated supporter of our campaign, I wanted to read you in on the details of that conversation.
Our Field Organizing operation is in overdrive, organizing across every corner of Texas. We’ve been busy knocking on hundreds of thousands of doors, calling and texting voters and volunteers, and registering as many eligible voters as possible before tomorrow’s big voter registration deadline. Our organizing plan will culminate in a massive voter turnout operation in the final days of this race.
**Nearly every recent poll is showing us within the margin of error against Greg Abbott.** The race will be close. And the size and strength of our get-out-the-vote campaign is what will decide whether we can hold onto our lead, or whether we fall short.
**[Our Field Director just told me the team urgently needs more support — so I’m turning to you to ask if you’ll make your first $5 donation to support our Organizing team.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261004_1_organizing.uSi0DU&refcode=em20261004-2311&amount=5&t=1&akid=2311%2E299639%2EeQkVtV)**
I know my team and I come to you a lot to ask for money. I by no means expect people to chip in every time I ask. But if you’re in a position to make a contribution today, it’d go a long way.

The Next AI Bottleneck Isn’t the Chip. It’s the Wire — and the Money Is Moving to Light.
While the world argued about an AI bubble, Nvidia quietly committed billions to companies that move data with light instead of copper. Here’s why the biggest player in AI is betting on photonics, and why most investors haven’t noticed.
Threat level 3/5 — Guarded
| | | | | | | | |

Most of the AI debate is about chips: who makes the fastest GPU, who gets the next shipment. But inside the world’s biggest data centers, engineers are fighting a different battle. The problem is no longer how fast a chip can think. It’s how fast thousands of chips can talk to each other. The answer the industry is betting on is light.
The bottleneck
| | Why Copper Is Running Out of Road
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
Today, most signals inside AI systems travel over copper. As data rates climb, copper loses signal quality and burns more power. It still works inside a single server rack, but it struggles across multiple racks. Nvidia’s planned Vera Rubin Ultra NVL576 links 576 GPUs across eight racks: copper inside the racks, optical links between them.
| OUR THEORY
---
Every leap in AI model size means more chips working as one machine. That machine is only as fast as its slowest connection. Once the connections become the limit, whoever controls the fastest, coolest-running links controls the next phase of the buildout.

Case File No DRT-ED-AI · Special File · The AI Fingerprint
1929\. 2000. 2008. We Found the Same Fingerprint on the AI Boom.
Record spending, $1.2 trillion in AI-linked debt plus hundreds of billions more off the books, a market resting on a few names, and Washington insisting it’s a golden age. History has seen this setup before. It rarely ends quietly.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Every financial crisis of the last hundred years left the same fingerprint before it hit. Prices ran far ahead of profits. Borrowing hid in places regulators weren’t looking. Fewer and fewer stocks carried the market. And the people closest to the boom kept insisting this time was different. We went looking for that fingerprint in the AI trade. Here’s what’s on the evidence board.
The pattern
| | Three Crashes, One Shape
---|---
| | 1929
---
The margin boom
Stocks bought with borrowed money, a market that only went up, and officials who called the economy sound. The Dow eventually lost close to 90% from its peak.
| | 2000
---
The dot-com bubble
Investment in tech hit record highs while profits lagged far behind. The Nasdaq fell about 78% from March 2000 to October 2002.
| | 2008
---
The leverage crisis
Debt was buried in off-balance-sheet vehicles most investors never saw. When it surfaced, bank stocks lost most, and in some cases all, of their value.
The evidence board
| | What the AI Boom Looks Like Right Now
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the spending.** Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta are on track to spend roughly $700 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026, mostly data centers and chips. In early 2026, Goldman Sachs pointed to peak investment spending as the first warning sign from the dot-com era.
| ██ REDACTED ██
---
**Exhibit B — the hidden debt.** A draft Treasury analysis obtained by NOTUS in July put visible AI-related corporate debt at about $1.2 trillion, roughly 14% of JPMorgan’s investment-grade index. It cited Moody’s estimate of $662 billion in data-center leases held off balance sheet through special-purpose vehicles funded by private credit. Treasury called the draft “unvetted.”
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the cash squeeze.** The same analysis projects hyperscalers will plow about 94% of their operating cash flow back into infrastructure by 2026–2027. This week Micron posted a record quarter and its stock still slipped after it announced higher spending: roughly $25 billion in capex in half a year.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit D — the thinning market.** Fewer than half of S&P; 500 stocks trade above their 200-day moving average, down from about 75% in mid-August. The index looks healthy only because a handful of leaders are holding it up.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit E — the cost of money.** In 1999 the Fed cut rates and fueled the rally. In 2026 the Fed has hiked, and the 10-year Treasury hit its highest level since 2002 this week. Every dollar of AI debt now costs more to carry.
Decoder
| | The Line Every Bubble Uses
---|---
| | “Artificial intelligence will be a key driver of America’s new Golden Age.”— Treasury spokesperson, responding to the draft report on AI debt
---|---
What it says
There’s nothing to worry about.
What it means
**Our theory:** AI may well transform the economy, and that’s exactly the problem. The internet did transform the economy, and the Nasdaq still lost 78%. A technology can be real and still be badly overpriced. When officials answer a warning about debt with a promise about the future, they’re not answering the question.

---|---
A major AI borrower struggles to refinance as yields stay above 5% **35%**
| |
---|---
A hyperscaler cuts its capex plan, and suppliers sell off together **30%**
| |
---|---
Private-credit losses tied to data-center leases surface publicly **20%**
| |
---|---
None of these by year-end: the boom keeps running **15%**
| |
---|---
Our best guesses. The four add up to 100%.
| ClassificationPressure, building
---
The fingerprint is there: record spending, debt hidden off balance sheet, a narrowing market, rising rates and official reassurance. None of that tells you the day the turn comes. It tells you the kind of protection people wished they’d had in 2000 and 2008 is worth looking at before the turn, not after.
| The riddle · answer at the end of the fileIn 2000 and in 2008, the warning signs were public for months. Why did so few investors act on them in time?
---
|
---
Riddle answer
**Because the crowd was still making money.** Warnings sound foolish while prices are rising, and the people who issue them get laughed at, right up until they don’t. **Our theory:** the investors who came through 2000 and 2008 intact didn’t predict the exact day. They decided in advance what they would do when the signals lined up. The signals are lining up now.

body:
Good day,

Once again, thank you for reaching out after seeing our Lauren 4 Congress campaign. I apologize for the delayed response;
campaign travel and weather have kept us extremely busy.

Our schedule for today is outlined below. Please feel free to come out, or text me at the number below so we can arrange
a time to meet after 9 am. Lauren and I would be glad to connect with you.

Today's Schedule:

\- 8:00 AM – 3:00 PM: Goodnight neighborhood area from 8 am to 9 am @ Fresh Doughnuts, 7930 Thaxton, 78747 (flexible
schedule for volunteer meet-and-greets, block walking, and planning /preparing for the upcoming deployments)

\- 3:45 PM – 6:00 PM: Ani's Day & Night (7107 East Riverside Drive, Austin, TX 78741 | <https://anisdayandnight.com/>)

We look forward to meeting you soon.

Best regards,

Sandy Ramirez McNaul
Campaign Coordinator
Lauren B. Peña for Congress CD37
Austin, Texas
[lauren4congress.com](http://lauren4congress.com/)

P.S. Texting is the quickest way to reach me.

# [PA Licensed Daycares Must Accept Unvaccinated Children](https://bethfarnhamforcongress.com/2026/10/04/pa-licensed-daycares-must-accept-unvaccinated-children/?jetpack_skip_subscription_popup)
---
By **Elizabeth Farnham** on October 4, 2026
---
| **District Round-up 10.04.26**
---
Dear Neighbor, Thank you for reading my District Round-up. As your candidate for Pennsylvania’s 13th Congressional District, it is my honor and pleasure to deliver to you where I’ve been and what issues I’ve tackled in the past week. Criss-crossing the counties of Adams, Franklin, Fulton, Bedford, Cambria, Blair, Huntingdon, Mifflin, Juniata, Perry, Cumberland, and Somerset gives me great opportunities to meet with voters, hear what is on your hearts and minds, and the chance to voice my fight for Everyday Americans. If you would like to contribute to my campaign, please donate here:**[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/beth-farnham-for-congress-1](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=48d511a6b8be3b57236b9e60b2d2931b3da93a0a3a286e31957c3e6498cf1a48&blog_id=213069660&post_id=9179&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=9ad141eac0360aa176cbfc9032a29c1e&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL2JldGgtZmFybmhhbS1mb3ItY29uZ3Jlc3MtMQ=&email_id=de280cc9bff2698e710b2838a1f5cdce)**
---
| **PA Licensed Daycares Must Accept Unvaccinated Children**
---
| |
---
Did you know that Pennsylvania licensed daycares must accept the signed statement of parents who believe antivaccine claptrap, and still admit the children?
---
That’s right, Pennsylvania Parents, the children of antivaxxers may very well walk or crawl the halls of the licensed daycare who demanded your child’s immunization record as part of the admission process.
---
You don’t know which children in the building don’t have their shots.
---
But antivaxxer parents knew to ask for the exemption form.
---
You only know that your dear child has as many boosters as their young age will permit under the vaccine schedule recommended by the American Association of Pediatrics (AAP).
---
And if your child is under a year old, they most likely haven’t had their first measles shot.
---
Oh sure, in the midst of an outbreak a school or daycare might not admit the unvaccinated children, but timing is everything and some diseases don’t show symptoms until the child has already spread it.
---
Antivaxxers don’t care if their kids suffer measles, mumps, polio, chicken pox, meningococcus, rubella, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), Hepatitus B, Hepatitus A, Rotavirus, Diphtheria, Whooping cough, the Flu, Human Papillomavirus, and COVID 19.
---
Antivaxxers don’t care if your kids suffer them either.
---
In fact, most haven’t told you their kids don’t have their shots. And if they can sell you some snake oil to cure what ails ya, they can profit from widespread disease and ignorance.
---
But it doesn’t have to be this way.
---
You can ask other parents what their vaccine philosophy is, then make decisions about who your children play with.
---
You can also vote for legislators at the state and federal level to stand up for science and stop mandating licensed daycares to admit unvaccinated children.
---
(Children whose parents follow the AAP recommended schedule of shots are likely to be fully immunized against the major diseases and can readily attend kindergarten as they are likely to be immunized enough to be in the general population. Obviously, none of this applies to the children who suffer medical conditions and literally can’t be vaccinated. We vaccinate our children to protect not only ours but the medically fragile ones too.)
---
Please vote for me, Beth Farnham, on November 3rd, so I can vote to stop daycares from accepting children who are not fully vaccinated, except for medically-fragile children, according to the AAP schedule.
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and the good health of our children!
---

Thank you, Jack, for carrying the banner with me!

#GooseDemocracy!
---
| | **Like the Cornell 7, Purity Culture Compares Females to Trash**
---
|
---
Why does my fight for Reproductive Freedom include national standards for sexuality education?
---
Because the “Cornell 7” happens when schools teach that girls and women are as disposable as trash.
---
In many unvetted “Sex Ed” classes, such as those taught by Crisis Pregnancy Centers (CPCs), there is often the “tape” lesson.
---
The premise is simple – each girl receives a piece of scotch tape and is encouraged to stick it onto the shirts or sweaters of as many boys as possible. After much giggling, everyone returns to their seats.
---
Then the girls are asked what’s different about the piece of tape.
---
The answers vary from, “It doesn’t work anymore” to “It doesn’t stick anymore” to “It’s worthless.”
---
The lesson?
---
If a young woman is with too many young men, she will lose her worth.
---
In fact the awful, religiously-based, sex ed that I worked with others to remove from two public school districts in 2019 was titled, “Project Worth.”
---
This is the kind of miseducation that contributes to the Cornell 7 and the like.
---
At the federal level we can institute national standards of sexuality education that are comprehensive, LGBTQ+-inclusive, and rooted in evidence -based science.
---
Please vote for me Beth Farnham so I can work with other caring legislators to provide quality instruction about consent, anatomy, contraception, sexually-transmitted infections, and more in ways that especially don’t demean girls and women.
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and real education!
---
(I’m also adding my write-up of the pitiful excuse of a sex ed “lesson” I was invited to observe in 2019.)
---
Sources: [https://www.washingtonpost.com/style/2026/09/30/three-most-chilling-words-cornell-rape-case-texts/?utm_source=newsshowcase&utm_medium=gnews&utm_campaign=CDAqDwgAKgcICjCO1JQKMLfRdDDl6bYF&utm_content=rundown&gaa_at=g&gaa_n=AXbw80Rkwn6eOBsMhNBtxCB3d96ZyqAASkLhdCwWKQLO-RAnMR5fmnx589M1CJnOtPtpuBZ1GAhvbdvkZYowHrZw-5Xjmg5d5w%3D%3D&gaa_ts=6abdce88&gaa_sig=eNHjbDsMGb-QzRD0MgDg27-YE-aYdG8FVnHGvrod_2oYln5N3bnGggfyV4MpG7xyae3HG20wvtXU9HhczRZCaQ%3D%3D&fbclid=IwY2xjawUv6zhleHRuA2FlbQIxMABwZG9mAWJyaWQRMTBIenU2Y2M1ekJqU0FwcjVzcnRjBmFwcF9pZBAyMjIwMzkxNzg4MjAwODkyAAEeTzyfOaSHF2uJmf3zkUl3ffV7LtrccQ0_kV6-e4k6SkSNTvSUEemClQhNwz4_aem_tc_E_5fCU_jlfYu4gL-_Tw](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=c4b41d85d619f92eb4e2793db2613ba4dc845d06bb9b142942e39fddf24427f5&blog_id=213069660&post_id=9179&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=2beaa69f00f04c3203c263bfe22fc52c&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=de280cc9bff2698e710b2838a1f5cdce)
---
[https://siecus.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/NSES-2020-2.pdf](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=e402a5bd464e9ffeff00ae72147508eb5bdbedbcba3a44b5c021dc856103999d&blog_id=213069660&post_id=9179&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=d99e251ea0c9c02bdec467872d30c52d&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9zaWVjdXMub3JnL3dwLWNvbnRlbnQvdXBsb2Fkcy8yMDIwLzAzL05TRVMtMjAyMC0yLnBkZg=&email_id=de280cc9bff2698e710b2838a1f5cdce)
---
Assessment of the Project W.O.R.T.H. Lesson

---
First, I’d like to note that the students at New Oxford Middle School, whom I observed in Mr. DeFelippo’s 8th grade, 4th period health class on Friday, March 1, 2019 ( a shortened period, due to a weather delay), were a delight to watch as they engaged, participated, and volunteered throughout the lesson. I have no issue with the students of CVSD. Also I’d like to note that this assessment is not to disparage the character of Mrs. Janczyk, but to highlight the egregiousness of the use of Tender Care’s materials and agents during instructional time.
---
Not having been given a lesson plan to follow along the lesson with, I was promptly seated at the back of the classroom and began to take notes with pen and paper. Mr. DeFelippo opened the lesson by going around and checking homework. He also commended students for their respect toward Mrs. Janczyk and then he stepped aside. This raised the first and basic question that was never satisfactorily answered throughout the lesson – why is the certified secondary education instructor relegated to simply checking homework, passing out papers, ending the lesson with a reminder about the next homework and deferring to an outsourced agent whose agency’s mission and values are focused less on science and much more on their Statement of Faith? Presumably Mr. DeFelippo and the other health teachers were hired due to their credentials including, but not limited to: college degrees of bachelor’s or higher in specific content areas including methods of teaching courses in his area of concentration, scores from teacher assessments like the Praxis series, experience in teaching, copies of previous observations, and any other life experiences that positively contribute to their teaching, as well as having passed rounds of interviews with CVSD personnel. Furthermore, it is assumed that Mr. DeFelippo takes continuing education to ensure his continued credentials. This raised other questions that were also never satisfactorily answered – what special expertise does Mrs. Janczyk possess beyond that of any certified secondary education health teacher?
---
With no identifiable written objective, Mrs. Janczyk opened her part of the lesson with the statement “We’re going to talk today about important topics. We’re going to talk about consent.” The importance of consent was announced repeatedly throughout the lesson, despite the fact Day 3 of Eighth Grade especially, was not a lesson about consent, nor did the activities and stated importance of the lesson match the materials about Project W.O.R.T.H. that I had been previously given to review. The constant reminders of how important a topic this is combined with the specific activities and transparencies provided, inconsistent with the previous Project W.O.R.T.H. materials I had reviewed raised the next question – was this lesson newly created since I, along with other parents raised the issue about a substantial lack of teaching consent?
---
Mrs. Janczyk then directed students to anonymously write down what they thought of the topic, if they thought consent was important and why, and directed students to put them in the container, in order to establish a baseline of student understanding before beginning the lesson, but this raised yet another question – would Mrs. Janczyk expand upon and ensure individual mastery of concepts beyond this basic level of understanding?
---
Mrs. Janczyk then verbally defined consent, but despite the importance of this topic, she did not direct students to write down the definition she gave, she did not have it written on the board for them to copy, and she did not direct them to one in the packet, if it existed. After asking general questions about sexual consent and fielding student’s verbal answers, she posted the No/Yes transparency on the board and verbally went over it, not directing students to copy it, not directing students to any possible corresponding worksheet in the packet if it existed, and not validating any other examples that students may have provided by also writing them on the transparency.
---
In asking about the #Metoo movement, Mrs. Janczyk verbally received a base level of student understanding and offered one local example of sexual assault. By focusing on college students in a dorm situation, Mrs. Janczyk missed multiple opportunities to cite several examples which are more appropriate considering the ages of the students. According to an AP analysis of federal crime data, requoted by the NEA in their article [http://neatoday.org/2017/12/04/sexual-assault-in-schools/](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=46377730e97068fbfca3336d7c5f20550c67d22e23103532a97b5e011d8de094&blog_id=213069660&post_id=9179&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=21c4aa78e969105fed8da7ca2b9300f7&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cDovL25lYXRvZGF5Lm9yZy8yMDE3LzEyLzA0L3NleHVhbC1hc3NhdWx0LWluLXNjaG9vbHMv&email_id=de280cc9bff2698e710b2838a1f5cdce) “While occasions of adult-on-child sexual assaults on school property claim headlines—and rightfully so—the problem of student-on-student sexual attacks is much more common. For every adult-on-child sexual assault, there were seven such assaults by students”.
---
Mrs. Janczyk also failed to mention local examples concerning adults in public secondary schools assaulting students.
---

Reading student answers from the papers and verbally validating their responses, Mrs. Janczyk used the word “coerced” and defined it verbally, but did not define it in writing and did not define other vocabulary related to non-consent such as bribery and intimidation. While she mentioned sexual assault, she did not provide applicable law about statutory rape, statutory exclusion, or “Romeo and Juliet” laws of Pennsylvania. When teaching about such an important topic, especially involving behaviors that could potentially carry legal jeopardy, it is important to provide relevant specifics.
---
After requesting two student volunteers to walk a straight line, Mrs. Janczyk then provided Fatal Vision alcohol impairment goggles for them to wear, explaining that each pair of goggles simulated “the vision of being drunk”. A quick glance at the website for the makers of the drunk goggles reveals that they are intended for the wearer, in order to simulate the experience of navigating while drunk. Therefore, only two students used the products as intended. While it is important for students to identify when an impaired person is incapable of giving informed consent, this demonstration in navigation was a weak correlation. Demonstrating physical impairment in terms of balance and equilibrium does not correlate to simulating impaired judgement. Additionally, Mrs. Janczyk noted the simulated alcohol blood content levels at .07 and higher. Pennsylvania law allows people under the age of 21 to be charged with a D.U.I. when BAC levels are as low as .02 which would have been timely to acknowledge. Not acknowledging these things was yet another indication of Mrs. Janczyk not considering the age of the students whom she was trying to teach. Time would have been better spent if she, the adult with presumably more experience regarding sex and alcohol, had provided scenarios based in a reality that she or other adults had experienced, for students to act out and for other students to determine if they were witnessing examples of consent and if not, what types of persuasion like coercion, intimidation, bullying, extortion, etc.
---
Throughout the lesson Mrs. Janczyk used awkward phrasing and weak transitions such as “Very interesting when you add the element of alcohol”, “There’s a lot to say when someone is drinking. How do you put consent together in a party scene?” ,“How do you know about dating violence?”, and “When you match the pornography with alcohol, you don’t have self-control” indicating an unfamiliarity with the subject. In my opinion, Mrs. Janczyk also conveyed a lack of professionalism by referring to one student as “Sweetheart” and stating to another “You’re smart. What do you think?”
---
Outside of mentioning that she had known people who were gang-raped, Mrs. Janczyk did not convey expertise beyond that of the established secondary education teacher. Additionally, Mrs. Janczyk failed to make a strong correlation, if any, that consent honors the simple “no” of abstinence. Mrs. Janczyk also stated “People don’t want to go through a court scene or have people found guilty.” This statement undermines the point of the previous conversation about the #Metoo movement and Mrs. Janczyk missed an exceptional opportunity to highlight the bravery of a local student who recently approached her high school counselor about an illicit sexual relationship that a man from Conewago Township had with her beginning when she was twelve years old.
---
[https://www.eveningsun.com/story/news/2018/12/14/police-conewago-township-man-arrested-after-having-sexual-contact-minor-two-years-hanover-pa/2311052002](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=e8be31619c90e4d2574ab116e9c735ae88acf77aae282a92e4a26412003d6286&blog_id=213069660&post_id=9179&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=42c2022d1509f509a2fca6541f95ed0a&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZXZlbmluZ3N1bi5jb20vc3RvcnkvbmV3cy8yMDE4LzEyLzE0L3BvbGljZS1jb25ld2Fnby10b3duc2hpcC1tYW4tYXJyZXN0ZWQtYWZ0ZXItaGF2aW5nLXNleHVhbC1jb250YWN0LW1pbm9yLXR3by15ZWFycy1oYW5vdmVyLXBhLzIzMTEwNTIwMDI&email_id=de280cc9bff2698e710b2838a1f5cdce)
---
Instead, Mrs. Janczyk turned the lesson back to the Tender Care packet for a few minutes to read over some signs of unhealthy relationships. Time would have been better spent by Mrs. Janczyk showing a video about consent, such as [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fGoWLWS4-kU](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=baf50cebd96226d459ce32a8acb15f98fb45db73e7ac9ff1afb1bc72f233e685&blog_id=213069660&post_id=9179&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=8181b0001358a2a6c573d7f299627628&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj1mR29XTFdTNC1rVQ=&email_id=de280cc9bff2698e710b2838a1f5cdce) or [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=laMtr-rUEmY](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=d704e40db6653078074278b8d507d760b81b35578e490de94ea0aa1d11d39838&blog_id=213069660&post_id=9179&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=b4d899f6eab74ae6c460b15cc1d99eaa&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj1sYU10ci1yVUVtWQ=&email_id=de280cc9bff2698e710b2838a1f5cdce)
---
While the students engaged in a group activity of answering questions about identifying boundaries, etc. (1) When should you have this conversation? 2) What should you ask?3) What, if anything, do you want to be clear about?), it was questionable for a couple of reasons. First, consent is a very abstract topic. By not establishing concrete scenarios, students were asked to imagine sexual scenarios and then the types of questions they might ask. Second, considering the relatively little sexual experience these students have presumably had, students would likely have little of their own concrete information to draw upon. While the students did participate in the activity, answers vacillated between generalized and speculative.
---
In directing the class to the written homework assignment she reminded students and their parents to write down what they would do in certain scenarios and requested a parent signature. Mrs. Janczyk said about the homework “Work with Mom and Dad – I need their input”. Why did Mrs. Janczyk state that she would need parental input? What happens if a student or parent shares views that are contrary to the express, explicit, and published views of Tender Care?
---
Student work was either collected in a container or it was displayed on the board, not to be taken home or even copied, but presumably, thrown away, calling in to question how much she truly valued student input.
---
A better homework assignment would have been for students to log two situations in which they were asked to give permission to someone else for something, and at least three situations in which they asked someone else for permission to do something, then to record how each situation went. This would have allowed students to explore consent situations in their own lives, to consciously practice it, or remind themselves of times that they already use it, and think critically about how they are persuaded, as well as how they persuade others.
---
In summary, the lack of follow-through, the missed opportunities to cite actual laws or examples more relevant to the age of her student audience, the failure to clearly define terms, especially in any written form, the inability to establish having moved students to a level beyond that of their original understanding, and the inability to establish individual student mastery of concepts, all converge to one conclusion – that Mrs. Janczyk, effectively, didn’t teach. Sure, she said some of the right things and the students were clearly engaged, but with four adults in the room, how much control of the class did she truly manage? Having observed this lesson, I am more affirmed of my position – that the Tender Care program, materials, representatives, and messages must be removed from instructional time in our public schools and replaced with the qualified instructors already in the classrooms presenting a truly comprehensive evidence-based sex ed program.
---

Lesson First, I’d like to note that the students at New Oxford Middle School, whom I observed in Mr. DeFelippo’s 8th grade, 4th period health class on Friday, March 1, 2019 ( a shortened period, due to a weather delay), were a delight to watch as they engaged, participated, and volunteered throughout the lesson. I have no issue with the students of CVSD. Also I’d like to note that this assessment is not to disparage the character of Mrs. Janczyk, but to highlight the egregiousness of the use of Tender Care’s materials and agents during instructional time. Not having been given a lesson plan to follow along the lesson with, I was promptly seated at the back of the classroom and began to take notes with pen and paper. Mr. DeFelippo opened the lesson by going around and checking homework. He also commended students for their respect toward Mrs. Janczyk and then he stepped aside. This raised the first and basic question that was never satisfactorily answered throughout the lesson – why is the certified secondary education instructor relegated to simply checking homework, passing out papers, ending the lesson with a reminder about the next homework and deferring to an outsourced agent whose agency’s mission and values are focused less on science and much more on their Statement of Faith? Presumably Mr. DeFelippo and the other health teachers were hired due to their credentials including, but not limited to: college degrees of bachelor’s or higher in specific content areas including methods of teaching courses in his area of concentration, scores from teacher assessments like the Praxis series, experience in teaching, copies of previous observations, and any other life experiences that positively contribute to their teaching, as well as having passed rounds of interviews with CVSD personnel. Furthermore, it is assumed that Mr. DeFelippo takes continuing education to ensure his continued credentials. This raised other questions that were also never satisfactorily answered – what special expertise does Mrs. Janczyk possess beyond that of any certified secondary education health teacher? With no identifiable written objective, Mrs. Janczyk opened her part of the lesson with the statement “We’re going to talk today about important topics. We’re going to talk about consent.” The importance of consent was announced repeatedly throughout the lesson, despite the fact Day 3 of Eighth Grade especially, was not a lesson about consent, nor did the activities and stated importance of the lesson match the materials about Project W.O.R.T.H. that I had been previously given to review. The constant reminders of how important a topic this is combined with the specific activities and transparencies provided, inconsistent with the previous Project W.O.R.T.H. materials I had reviewed raised the next question – was this lesson newly created since I, along with other parents raised the issue about a substantial lack of teaching consent? Mrs. Janczyk then directed students to anonymously write down what they thought of the topic, if they thought consent was important and why, and directed students to put them in the container, in order to establish a baseline of student understanding before beginning the lesson, but this raised yet another question – would Mrs. Janczyk expand upon and ensure individual mastery of concepts beyond this basic level of understanding? Mrs. Janczyk then verbally defined consent, but despite the importance of this topic, she did not direct students to write down the definition she gave, she did not have it written on the board for them to copy, and she did not direct them to one in the packet, if it existed. After asking general questions about sexual consent and fielding student’s verbal answers, she posted the No/Yes transparency on the board and verbally went over it, not directing students to copy it, not directing students to any possible corresponding worksheet in the packet if it existed, and not validating any other examples that students may have provided by also writing them on the transparency. In asking about the #Metoo movement, Mrs. Janczyk verbally received a base level of student understanding and offered one local example of sexual assault. By focusing on college students in a dorm situation, Mrs. Janczyk missed multiple opportunities to cite several examples which are more appropriate considering the ages of the students. According to an AP analysis of federal crime data, requoted by the NEA in their article “While occasions of adult-on-child sexual assaults on school property claim headlines—and rightfully so—the problem of student-on-student sexual attacks is much more common. For every adult-on-child sexual assault, there were seven such assaults by students”. Mrs. Janczyk also failed to mention local examples concerning adults in public secondary schools assaulting students. Reading student answers from the papers and verbally validating their responses, Mrs. Janczyk used the word “coerced” and defined it verbally, but did not define it in writing and did not define other vocabulary related to non-consent such as bribery and intimidation. While she mentioned sexual assault, she did not provide applicable law about statutory rape, statutory exclusion, or “Romeo and Juliet” laws of Pennsylvania. When teaching about such an important topic, especially involving behaviors that could potentially carry legal jeopardy, it is important to provide relevant specifics. After requesting two student volunteers to walk a straight line, Mrs. Janczyk then provided Fatal Vision alcohol impairment goggles for them to wear, explaining that each pair of goggles simulated “the vision of being drunk”. A quick glance at the website for the makers of the drunk goggles reveals that they are intended for the wearer, in order to simulate the experience of navigating while drunk. Therefore, only two students used the products as intended. While it is important for students to identify when an impaired person is incapable of giving informed consent, this demonstration in navigation was a weak correlation. Demonstrating physical impairment in terms of balance and equilibrium does not correlate to simulating impaired judgement. Additionally, Mrs. Janczyk noted the simulated alcohol blood content levels at .07 and higher. Pennsylvania law allows people under the age of 21 to be charged with a D.U.I. when BAC levels are as low as .02 which would have been timely to acknowledge. Not acknowledging these things was yet another indication of Mrs. Janczyk not considering the age of the students whom she was trying to teach. Time would have been better spent if she, the adult with presumably more experience regarding sex and alcohol, had provided scenarios based in a reality that she or other adults had experienced, for students to act out and for other students to determine if they were witnessing examples of consent and if not, what types of persuasion like coercion, intimidation, bullying, extortion, etc. Throughout the lesson Mrs. Janczyk used awkward phrasing and weak transitions such as “Very interesting when you add the element of alcohol”, “There’s a lot to say when someone is drinking. How do you put consent together in a party scene?” ,“How do you know about dating violence?”, and “When you match the pornography with alcohol, you don’t have self-control” indicating an unfamiliarity with the subject. In my opinion, Mrs. Janczyk also conveyed a lack of professionalism by referring to one student as “Sweetheart” and stating to another “You’re smart. What do you think?” Outside of mentioning that she had known people who were gang-raped, Mrs. Janczyk did not convey expertise beyond that of the established secondary education teacher. Additionally, Mrs. Janczyk failed to make a strong correlation, if any, that consent honors the simple “no” of abstinence. Mrs. Janczyk also stated “People don’t want to go through a court scene or have people found guilty.” This statement undermines the point of the previous conversation about the #Metoo movement and Mrs. Janczyk missed an exceptional opportunity to highlight the bravery of a local student who recently approached her high school counselor about an illicit sexual relationship that a man from Conewago Township had with her beginning when she was twelve years old. Instead, Mrs. Janczyk turned the lesson back to the Tender Care packet for a few minutes to read over some signs of unhealthy relationships. Time would have been better spent by Mrs. Janczyk showing a video about consent, such as or While the students engaged in a group activity of answering questions about identifying boundaries, etc. (1) When should you have this conversation? 2) What should you ask?3) What, if anything, do you want to be clear about?), it was questionable for a couple of reasons. First, consent is a very abstract topic. By not establishing concrete scenarios, students were asked to imagine sexual scenarios and then the types of questions they might ask. Second, considering the relatively little sexual experience these students have presumably had, students would likely have little of their own concrete information to draw upon. While the students did participate in the activity, answers vacillated between generalized and speculative. In directing the class to the written homework assignment she reminded students and their parents to write down what they would do in certain scenarios and requested a parent signature. Mrs. Janczyk said about the homework “Work with Mom and Dad – I need their input”. Why did Mrs. Janczyk state that she would need parental input? What happens if a student or parent shares views that are contrary to the express, explicit, and published views of Tender Care? Student work was either collected in a container or it was displayed on the board, not to be taken home or even copied, but presumably, thrown away, calling in to question how much she truly valued student input. A better homework assignment would have been for students to log two situations in which they were asked to give permission to someone else for something, and at least three situations in which they asked someone else for permission to do something, then to record how each situation went. This would have allowed students to explore consent situations in their own lives, to consciously practice it, or remind themselves of times that they already use it, and think critically about how they are persuaded, as well as how they persuade others. In summary, the lack of follow-through, the missed opportunities to cite actual laws or examples more relevant to the age of her student audience, the failure to clearly define terms, especially in any written form, the inability to establish having moved students to a level beyond that of their original understanding, and the inability to establish individual student mastery of concepts, all converge to one conclusion – that Mrs. Janczyk, effectively, didn’t teach. Sure, she said some of the right things and the students were clearly engaged, but with four adults in the room, how much control of the class did she truly manage? Having observed this lesson, I am more affirmed of my position – that the Tender Care program, materials, representatives, and messages must be removed from instructional time in our public schools and replaced with the qualified instructors already in the classrooms presenting a truly comprehensive evidence-based sex ed program. | Gettysburg History | | | Many thanks to Andrew Dalton of the Gettysburg History for presenting the Jack Hopkins house and rich history of its tenants to members and friends of the Daughters of the American Revolution (DAR) on Thursday. The Hopkins house has a special place in history because it’s the story of a Black community that begins with freedom. Right now the Hopkins house is under renovation, but the vision is clear – an historic house, preserved properly for generations of visitors to learn about. Black history is American history and I stand for its preservation (and restoration after the Trump administration). Please vote for me, Beth Farnham, so that the truth of our nation may never be buried. Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and History! | | ---|--- | Another Amazing Day in our 13th Congressional District | | Many thanks to the Borough of Huntingdon for holding Octoberfest and to the Newport Revitalization & Preservation Society for holding Canal Day on Saturday. It was a beautiful, sunny day to speak to voters from many parts of our gorgeous 13th Congressional district. While I staffed the tent in Huntingdon, Campaign Manager Jack staffed the one at Newport. Many thanks to Jack and our tremendous team of volunteers today – Deb, Janis, Kelley, Angie, and Chris – who engaged voters, set up and tore down tents, took pictures and boosted morale in general just by being there. Together, we ! | | | ---|---|--- | Continued Pain at the Pump | | How many more weeks are Americans going to have to suffer these sustained high prices? It’s not just one week of high prices, it’s MONTHS! And now people are buying their home heating oil at high prices. In the meantime, our stockpiles of weapons are dwindling, rendering our nation more vulnerable to our enemies! But our own US Representative, multimillionaire John Joyce, won’t vote to discontinue our hostilities in Iran. He doesn’t care what it costs Everyday Americans! Vote for me, Beth Farnham, instead of that elitist who only serves Trump’s ego. I’ll vote us out of Iran and vote for policies that benefit Everyday Americans like hardworking families and retirees on fixed incomes, instead of kowtowing to the ultra-wealthy. Together, we ! | Charity of the Week! Even though charitable donations will not meet the overwhelming need of food assistance and healthcare for lower income Americans, these charities are a stopgap until I am elected to the U.S. House of Representatives and can legislate helpful federal programs as well as prevent a rapacious president from illegally impounding the congressionally-approved funds for those programs. Please check out the United Way of Mifflin-Juniata page and donate to them, if you can. website – donation link – | | | Comparing and Contrasting Votes on Legislation Check out how Joyce recently voted, how I would have voted in comparison, and why! FYI – if you’re having trouble seeing this comparison in your email, please click the option for “Read on Blog” and it will load properly for you. | | If you’re like me, you love this country as much as I do and work to make a positive difference. In the midst of this Constitutional Crisis, please consider reaching out to your county Democratic committee or Democratic candidates so that we can strengthen our Democracy instead of letting it slide into fascism. We don’t just #ChooseDemocracy, we choose Pennsylvania, we choose The United States of America, we choose Humanity and I am deeply glad to work along side you. Roy

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Cook Political just shifted our race AGAIN
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Heartland Patriots (LucasKunce
body:
The independent analysts at the Cook Political Report shifted this race in our favor again.
This is a big deal, Peter. So I want you to hear this major news directly from me:
**The independent political analysts at the _Cook Political Report_ just shifted the Texas governor’s race in our favor... again!**
This is the second time in just two months that they’ve shifted their race rating towards Democrats. They’ve done it again just now because they know what we all know:
**Our momentum to unseat Greg Abbot is now undeniable.**
This move confirms what I’ve been seeing and hearing on the ground: Texans are ready to put an end to Abbott’s reign once and for all. I believe we will win if we can spread our message in these final 29 days until Election Day. But that all depends on what we can raise in pivotal moments like right now.
**[Please split a donation of $25 or more between Heartland Patriots and my campaign to help respond to this rating change and power our GOTV efforts in this final stretch. There has never been a more important moment for our campaign to see a surge in fundraising than today.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/109468?refcode=em20261005-10966&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=25&t=1&akid=10966%2E614464%2EIsbG88)**
If you only read one piece of political news today, please let it be this direct quote from the analysts at the _Cook Political Report:_
_Both public and private polling shows a tightening race, including GOP surveys that have shown the contest closing despite Abbott outspending Hinojosa by more than six to one on the airwaves._ _Abbott — who spent much of the race not even uttering Hinojosa's name — is now aggressively attacking her, showing the degree to which this contest has become fiercely competitive._
---
Greg Abbott is losing his grip on Texas. He knows it, Republican strategists know it, and you and I know it, too. **But he is responding by dumping tens of millions on false TV ads about me to try to win back support in these final four weeks.**
The *only* way this race stays in play is if we can keep our organizers on the ground and ads on the airwaves. We do not have to match Abbott’s spending dollar for dollar – we just need to raise enough to execute our strategy to mobilize the Texas voters we know will break in our favor.
**[Your support has never been more important than it is today. If you can, would you split $25 between Heartland Patriots and my campaign to power our campaign strategy to defeat Greg Abbott?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/109468?refcode=em20261005-10966&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=25&t=2&akid=10966%2E614464%2EIsbG88)**

**Today is Arizona’s, Texas’s, and Georgia’s voter registration deadline.**

**Nationwide, 1 in 3 young voters is unregistered.** So if we’re able to bridge that gap, just imagine the impact young, registered Latino voters can make in this critical election.

Hi Peter — I've got some really exciting news to share with you:
**Our campaign has been selected by The Democratic Party for its National Red to Blue program. This means we are one of the most competitive and viable campaigns in the fight to earn back the majority in the House.**
This is an incredible milestone made possible because of you!
We are one of a few candidates that national leaders believe can genuinely win Republican-leaning seats and gerrymandered districts.
This is proof of what we already believed: **folks outside TN-09 are watching our People-powered Movement, and they know we can win this race.**
We’re within four points of our Trump-endorsed opponent! **[Help us convert our momentum into victory by splitting a $10 donation between our campaign and Justice Democrats:](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261005-jjp.QhX4od&refcode=em20261005-38327&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=2&akid=38327%2E1203867%2E6iTdfR)**

Far-right Republicans rushed to redraw our district earlier this year for one reason: **to give Donald Trump a congressional seat before anyone had a chance to vote.** They drew the lines and expected this race to be a mere formality — handed over to his personal pick.
_But it’s not over._ We’re _so close_ , even on the map they drew to try and stop us.
**The next few weeks will be difficult, and I won’t pretend otherwise, Peter.** Trump-endorsed Brent Taylor won’t debate me. And that means the eight percent of voters who are still undecided will never see the two of us answer the same questions in the same room.
Our ads are the only place they’ll get to see that comparison. Keeping them on the air through Election Day is why we need to raise $50,000.

Justin J. Pearson

# Monday, October 5, 2026

**Good Morning!** On this day in 1921, the World Series went out live on radio for the first time, with the Giants and Yankees at the Polo Grounds. Fans without a ticket could follow a game as it happened. [Read how the broadcasts began here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1ygzAQhJ8GOhj9nCAUKtLQOW1KRsDJuuSEPJJsj98-Q6r0qXdnv9nv87JcHDEd1w8X0VaflgOfhbFWzMu93O7MZU1xxVx8TvH-HV2mY1FCDZ0UnTCL2yo9cAHX7tYjKtQtWjlOUk4wDFMb7Gg2AANvG4CWuBrQkxRoPGoltJbQkj33pBBGCgFq7Eexj9IMiKg97G5sQOBONeX-K9FRA3p-pQfmfkuxZRtqvZVGvzdqbtS8uoKrYw6OuU_52qh5p7Kd_T9pF6jUlF-NmiPGlAlLdz7sasAu0tZmu9-exExlOPnX6Ih_efWfmh5W_QQAAP__9cd-Rw). Forgetting where you parked is not the same as losing your memory. University of Arizona researchers argue the aging brain is not breaking down but reorganizing, giving up detail [in favor of the bigger picture](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGurCAYhJ9GOwyg4lJQ3Ga7ve0tDcKP_vcgGPhds29_4nmFU85kMjP5_r3ml8WIaf1rdzAU8pzgqhGIoMxnPc4Y65L3BUoNJe_n124LpllyqZjgjI-zdYRvmAfbehMAJPQtGDFpIfSglG43M_UPPoIWD_VwTnMIoKUXy-iUm6RyukVz9wnOR8H5IKdu4n4SowKAPgzeTs3AwSPl0v3PmGiDED_5DaVzeW-j2YiO2vR_Gvls5PO6rq46hOTARih0hxr5pA2YXTGtbCkWE8OaiHlwEdNtIlVmvT3oFpVO_2EBk69tMf64MEas6v6x7hbjzy79EtfbyO8AAAD__yPCgrM) it has built over time. We have details in _Science_. Remember the traditions you used to keep and somehow just stopped? A lot of the ones we grew up with are quietly slipping away, and the numbers on how far each has fallen are steeper than you'd expect. Which Sunday tradition did families once build the whole week around? And why are so few grooms asking their bride's father for permission anymore? In the latest episode of _Flyover Focus_ , we count down 10 American traditions that are fading, ending with the one you could still bring back before the month is out. [Tune in here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykz0Fu6yAUQNHVmFkseMYmDBh8fdWjptOoI4ThEdOCiQA7yu6rdAtdwD3SvV70xYQYttuHSaiaz3rDR43YGha91_seY11yWrBUX3Lav5MpYdNAYToxeqKjNraFAzU3xCmPCDgQVExIxiSfJklWJe0weBTnUUq3OGc9d1YKdHiWEiycSVAvj1E6Mko5iF5QJ9g4IeLguTOi4xRdaLn0XzlsbUUfn_nA0tucSFRra_faDf86mDuYn3lve79gB3P-P8P79dOb9Y0U5e6PEGOo08u7JRPib9_-uH0o-AkAAP__101tXg)! Today's sponsor, [Steven Gundry, MD](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0M1qhDAUBeCnibuRm6smusiiMNhNZ6A_0KVkzHUmbWIkiUrfvthX6PocvgPn8zJctHV2vl-1J5WnMMy0J0c5UxzWtKzOpVvwN4ppisGv315HOw8IKE4cTtAMesx2o6HWhVETEVJVkOKy47yrheiKhxo7ANOBINE0uoWxJUOtaJG0Ng3xsbDq8DhAwwFqlKUEI3kjiKiaaqMlq4GMzSGWX8HO-UGT-wkbxXIMvnDqkfOSWPXEsGfY7_teehMXykfMsH97ltfrmWFfvby_nj_wqFV9Wm-cVWcpURRRmWW3ztkkjq2719b92fmfl2wKfwMAAP__y8R0Ig), is sharing his research on a common dietary protein he believes may contribute to stubborn weight gain, cravings, and belly bloat, as well as what you may want to eat instead.

## Social Security Checks to Climb above $2,000

clean_body: The U.S. Air Force from RAF Fairford on Sunday, the British base used to strike Iran, a week after police arrested five men near it on suspicion of plotting an attack. | | | | | | Monday, October 5, 2026 ---|--- Good Morning! On this day in 1921, the World Series went out live on radio for the first time, with the Giants and Yankees at the Polo Grounds. Fans without a ticket could follow a game as it happened. . Forgetting where you parked is not the same as losing your memory. University of Arizona researchers argue the aging brain is not breaking down but reorganizing, giving up detail it has built over time. We have details in Science. Remember the traditions you used to keep and somehow just stopped? A lot of the ones we grew up with are quietly slipping away, and the numbers on how far each has fallen are steeper than you'd expect. Which Sunday tradition did families once build the whole week around? And why are so few grooms asking their bride's father for permission anymore? In the latest episode of Flyover Focus , we count down 10 American traditions that are fading, ending with the one you could still bring back before the month is out. ! Today's sponsor, , is sharing his research on a common dietary protein he believes may contribute to stubborn weight gain, cravings, and belly bloat, as well as what you may want to eat instead. | US Pulls All Bombers from UK Base The U.S. Air Force from RAF Fairford on Sunday, the British base used to strike Iran, a week after police arrested five men near it on suspicion of plotting an attack. A Pentagon spokesperson and said B-1, B-2, and B-52 crews can still deliver strikes anywhere, including on missions flown from the continental United States. British officials have not disputed that Washington acted in response to the incident, which was reportedly a made at an operational level rather than a political one. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there were "strong indications" Iran was involved, which Tehran denies. Six men have been arrested and released on bail, including a dual U.K.-Iranian national. Trump Creates Super Intelligence Force President Trump announced Sunday that he is creating a , a federal task force he says will keep America ahead on artificial intelligence while protecting Americans from its risks. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will chair the group, joined by the FTC chairman, the Pentagon's research chief, and the head of federal personnel. They have to report on the risks and opportunities of AI. The announcement follows a White House meeting last week where six AI companies signed a to police their own technology, which Trump called "morally binding." Clayton ran the Securities and Exchange Commission in Trump's first term and was confirmed as intelligence director in July. He will keep that job while chairing the task force, and told the media that "the risk of not being first is high." Social Security Checks to Climb above $2,000 The average Social Security check across all beneficiaries would climb above $2,000 a month next year under the 3.5% cost-of-living raise now , an increase of about $68. The estimate comes from the Senior Citizens League, an advocacy group. AARP puts it slightly higher at , which would add about $75 to the average retired worker's check. Neither number is official. The Social Security Administration sets the figure on Oct. 14, after the government releases September inflation data, and bases it on . body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2054%2E1086043%2EaEIs7_)
Peter, Wes is hoping you’ll answer this one-question survey before this week’s debate.
**What do you want to hear from Wes on the debate stage?**
**[Share With Wes »](https://act.wesmoore.com/signup/moore-2026-debate-survey/?refcode=em20261005-1&t=2&akid=2054%2E1086043%2EaEIs7_)**
We know how Dan Cox will spend his time on stage: lobbing attack after attack after Wes’ record.
Wes has bigger plans. He’s ready to actually get into the issues and discuss the progress we’ve made for Maryland, from raising the minimum wage to delivering paid family and medical leave.
Marylanders don’t want to hear name-calling and baseless attacks. We get enough of that from the White House.
Wes knows his time on stage belongs to the voters who are watching -- and he wants to know which issues folks like you are most focused on right now.
**What do you want to hear most from Wes on the debate stage?**
**[Share With Wes »](https://act.wesmoore.com/signup/moore-2026-debate-survey/?refcode=em20261005-1&t=3&akid=2054%2E1086043%2EaEIs7_)**
The choice on the debate stage will be clear to anyone who cares about Maryland’s future.
That’s why our team is working nonstop to organize volunteers and get our message out across Maryland. Together, we’ll win this re-election fight and keep building a state where we leave no one behind.
Thank you for making your voice heard.
-- Team Wes Moore for Maryland

## Lake Palestine Ranch Becomes State Park
The Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation [closed on 650 acres](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGuqzAQRVdjOqOxITgULn5Dl9--Eg14nFgxOMITnOz-CbbwuiuN7tHc83MbbxhiWO__cSHLH5_GlUqOxEzbGRmZXrg951Sm9M0TITONGnQnFUi4jDhz2GlssXJ2AteriqwyvVL9FUxTPWzXNg6u3jQeu94YBx16hZOapms7o8cq2AOnAC5KgVJQd1Mzo1Faz35uzMWJFsgFTlvND2L6YPbxm3ba6jktVbQP5lcWzT-hB6GHUkr9jLwfR6GHgy30oEDoAbTQwwmQx6YsS4guBk_Sp_fqkENaZVh3ypzlEmIMac3Sv_m9kTxVnD0Z8XmkSJnDSkIP1WbdqxyF3BnRwn3BEM_v-K9Wd6t_AwAA__9liY9n) along Lake Palestine in Henderson County on Oct. 1, paying more than $10 million for a ranch that will become a new state park. The tract sits [about 100 miles southeast of Dallas](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQRb_GdEZjA-ZRuEhD99KmRIM9LNYaG5nJsvv3ESj5gnQj3aurOefX9_SNIYb0-IkbWX4veUp0HpGYqdwnI9OO5enyOefPMRMy06RBG6lAQjeh4_CiqcXK2xn8oCqyqh-UGr6gb6rVtg4Vgmlm06Myplk0oAFqFTQe2s5VwV5zCqBTCpSC2syNw15p7RbX9J0XLZAPnEvNKzG98VjiJ7-o1C5vVbQr836I5ofQo9DjeZ51mp1fzisWerwwhB5jdhiFHj3GiIfcckkhPeS_FJ-0lJxYFkxulYmwyL_VM8QoZ3J5o6su7xfkrUZebiQuTOXysYUYQ05y_13cigcJPbbwZZQehB6rYv1-bYXD9KKFx4Yh3gj8v-pfVv8JAAD__2ZNm1o), roughly halfway between Chandler and Moore Station, in native pine forest and pasture. Plans call for hiking and biking trails, campsites, boating, and lakefront access. The foundation will invest more money in the property before handing it over to the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department [in late 2027](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OwyAQhU-DOyzAxsQFxTbusu2WFj9DgkKMBZPYuf3KlvYEW80njWb0vvdzna8mprjcvs0TNO4hzwtsNQEilBPRIKymPFzebP5UCwYRZsHEQDmjTM7GYXzD3JvGa8v8yBvQXI2cjxemuuauxehDL8HZi5KdFz3vpZXBggWrrGS2ifp4xxmTnDPOWTvYzhnFhXDBdUp60jPwEXNp8Q4Iu6khffIbSuvys0n6jrhW0n0RMRExbdvWPnazHEsipkOCiOk8-5u0gnsVqHSQjBp3UMiFhhe-CtDTmR7SFPbVLDXmhYipKdqvW0wp1kGRnt2eJqYzAf63ubcWvwEAAP__-NiF-g). The Pollard family has [owned the land since 1940](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykUL3OqzAUe5qwgU5-IM2Q4S5s313viA7hUKKmBIWjpn37q_IK32bZsi3738_0gzHF_f4Xn-T5veZpp3omYqZyQUamA8sj5DrnzzkTMtOkQA2thBb6CQPHF00Gm8XPsDjZkJfWSeluYHWz-dXdZmcG0jeCeTWmJ9Szc5Y0gNO9bKL_xkmAXkqQErph1gGtVCqsQdt-EQZoiZxLxxsxvfFc0ye_qHQhP5vkN-bjFPqPUKNQY621C1vJ-1cVarwMQo1YOIZEQo071fZi2--yNuGD2gMTnRx3apUyvR2M7Y7taIpfjhpTiudghYH7E2O6Wvm3b728-h8AAP__mgh_1Q), running the Texas Pecan Nursery on part of it, while most of it has remained untouched. "_I think they're really happy that it's going to be preserved forever_ ," listing broker Josh Smith said.
## Waxahachie Mother Charged in Sons' Deaths
Deputies who walked into a Waxahachie home before dawn Thursday, Oct. 1, [found two brothers shot](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLuu4yAQhp8Gd1iA7wXFNu6y7ZbWAOOAgoMFsyF5-yPnFU43mv-iT_-_23aDEMPz_hcO1PTe0_bEWiISYf6eBIQn5IdN1aRPMQhEuCmhRi4FF8MGlsILtx4ap41wi2xQy2mRcpnF1DVew2wm7MSwd2raTT_uvdvnYVj6ZVayt0MT9FUnhRikFFKKdjSdhUkqZXfbTYNjvUAXKOWWPBK-oezxk16YW5uOJmpPdBbW_WFqZWqttbbWlAv-0plavxGm1ut1GeANHqwPyI9EHjO3cAaCyI__2WHmVBMv6Vl48Yn4I8SIjidLyWDmFytTa5O1O2uIMZRxYr24HxDil4d-u-NLq58AAAD__88hilk) in the head in separate bedrooms, and their 42-year-old mother now faces two counts of capital murder. An arrest affidavit says deputies found Colleen Nichole Lemmon covered in blood, [a handgun beside her,](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOnDAQhJ8GOiOv4TAULtJcd2lTosVesBWDkb05uLePuFf4u0-a0ejT_HlNLwwx7Otv3MjwtaRpp7NEYqb8RUamA_Nfm845fcpMyEyTkqoXIIV8TGg5vGnqsHZmlm6EmgzoEWAcpG5rbxbdWivVMg_QgQU9DgN1ehmgp7brAepg7jmQ8gEgAWTTz61FDUrZxbb64apOkguccsOemC4sS_ykN-XGpq2OxjMfpWp_VepZqed5ns2Sru62vwuVet54J3ihR-sDiS2xpyysx7ySExaPwBjF9i87yqL4lDjsq3CE7IUSJe2lzsYdZ4gxlF5XnVw3DPFrwD997m3U_wAAAP__dm2GBw) and what appeared to be self-inflicted cuts on her wrists. Asked where the blood came from, she told them, "_I shot both my kids_." Christopher Scott Pitre, 21, was pronounced dead at the home on Big Sky Drive, and his 15-year-old brother died later at a hospital. Lemmon was treated, then booked into the Wayne McCollum Detention Center [on $2.5 million bond](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2O6zAQg09jdwpm5L-4UPGadHntlsZYGtnCypYhzcbJ7RfJFbYjQYIgvq_7dKcQw778p42NPH2adj5LZBHOHykkfFD-tumc06vMTCI8adC9QlDQTWQlPHhqqXZmBjdizQaHEXG8wtDUqxmRZwA3WkCPV9tTZ_0wtxZpbAbvdB3Mew4BOkRAhEs_N5YG1Np62wydq1pgFyTli6ws_KTi4ys9OF9s2upoVpGjVM2_St8qfTs4HZHfUaVvn7ba0qbsSnlhp84gq7J0BKGotp_sOKuwK09vX9aUJOyLSl5pVdJeFGrsumuv62zccYYYQ-mHqoVloxA_B-Sv4B5G_wYAAP__KiyEyA).
## Longhorn Who Outdueled Staubach Dies
Duke Carlisle, the quarterback who led Texas to [its first national championship](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL9u9CAQxJ8Gd1iA_xcUX-PuvjaltYa1jQ6DA5vz3dtHvihPkGpXv12NZubjNt3AeRfW_7CjpucSp4Bn9kiE6b0SEB6Q7iaec3zlGYEIJyVUy6XgopnAkHvgVENh9SzsIAvUshukHHrRVcWm5ayGBnsDnYGq7-WCII01UEODLcBQOH3JSSEaKYWUomznykAnlTKLqbrGslqgdRRTSRsSPiEv_hUfmEoT98LrjejIrPrH1MjUeJ5nGUN13ZgaCWHP7_mEzH0M6xZTuMiVjqnxF3GPKwbLF5cy8Z_3AORiAM_NBvvhYsibO_jnzO3XHbmB5F32yA_IGTOHE15MjUXS9jid9y63HavFuoPzb6f014YfWn0HAAD__zEBlgU) and took MVP honors in the 1964 Cotton Bowl, died Friday in Lockhart at 84 after a battle with lung cancer. Carlisle was born in Kaufman, grew up in Athens, and worked as an [investment banker in New York](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO2zAQBNCvoToa3JUsWQWLNOwubUphSa5OxFGiQm7s898H9i9cN8AAD4P587F8UMrp-PxNO1v5Xsty8KNlFuH6jkLCJ9WvUB6-PJtnEuEFDY4ajDbXhYKkOy8DddF6E2fo2MI0A8w3M_XdZo3nvkee4LZeYYo4Axnvwww498OIY5fsiwNjrgAGwFxG3weaADGsoZ-uUQ2GY5JSL7Kx8De1NT_LnesllL3LdhM5m-p_KXQK3fE8S5NXpdC9ZIUOjEJneoWunaVKU-jWUneu-s3pgySVg7IOG-1nKkfb0qn_eh3_fbEOVHNqmXVkippE3waFrqs2no-Uc2rjpAbzuVPK70Xy0yfvFv8HAAD__8wgiE4) before landing in the oil business in Mississippi. In the Cotton Bowl on Jan. 1, 1964, Carlisle threw for [a then-record 234 yards](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1ywyAQhJ9G6qQ5QIiooEijzmlTag44W4yRUODin7fP2K-QbovdnW--79NywpjifvnCjSw_znnZ6V4TMVN5R0amA8vV57vLz-oImWmRIMdOQAd6Qc_xRsuAbbAOwiRassJMQkwfYFS7Wqm8CIakG8OoNbiJQBtDYJwKeqCpjfZ1JwC0ECAE9KNTHo2Q0p-9Mjo0A1CInEvPKzE9sJ7TM9-o9D5vbbIr81Eb9dnIuZFzPXLh2j9xzflVaOSMhaNPVBs5v-fdjhzzjqnzK25HzHtd49H9_GJhKg79tQuEoRNKaT1IpfqVt9QWG457TCnW0TQDXDaM6Y3A_1V3s_IvAAD__wFphas), and two long touchdowns to Phil Harris as Texas beat Roger Staubach's No. 2 Navy 28-6. Carlisle played safety, too, and his end-zone interception against Baylor, the only defensive series he played all season, preserved a 7-0 win and kept Texas unbeaten. He entered [the Longhorn Hall of Honor](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDHOozAQhU9jOkceE3AoXGxDl223RGN7ACsORvZsSG6_ItKe4O--4tPMe-_PfbpjTHFbfuOTLL_nPG101ETMVL7IyLRjefh8uPypjpCZJq10L0FJ1U3oOb5oumITrFNhgIYsmAFguCnTNqu9Bd_5bjBOB_BIPRozOOh113ZuQFRNtOc5UKoDUADq0rvWowGt_exb0wVxVRQi53LhlZjeWOf0yS8qF5-fTbIr815F-0voUejxK6S8LWsuWz0VocezitDj-UjoEdTJQo9zzuwwJfnfl4kW2oIMfx8kPZYUayK5Y61UJR74aYoN-xFTirU34qqWJ8b0zcE_3e9l9b8AAAD__yfzhuQ) in 1979.
| _Flying together with our sponsor_ [](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2L4zAQhn-N3MVoJEeOChWBYLgid83BbifG8igRq1jBno2Tf7_Y22273TMfvDy8b2d_xpTTePmLN3L8jMWPtMyZmGnakJHpjtNHKEtfXnNPyExeSWV2IHdy7zFwepBvsBpcLwcLFTloLYA9yFZXV2d01AZba3qLbWzANlqrcFCANsTGhCq5NQ6k3ANIAFmbXgdsQakQg273g2gkDYnLVPOVmJ44x_wqD5rqUG5Vdlfm-yz0UahOqG5ZlvpCXKYUMq0f61p3nqLnCcd5FS6jT4PQJ6FM2QDA_mCMcZuU1kKZ-bMHoU__37t_Qplj9-f0faomN9yXlHOaTSsaeblhypsW_7bOh1NfAQAA___toIXB) **This Tiny Hearing Aid Is Changing Lives --[And It's Under $100](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2L4zAQhn-N3MVoJEeOChWBYLgid83BbifG8igRq1jBno2Tf7_Y22273TMfvDy8b2d_xpTTePmLN3L8jMWPtMyZmGnakJHpjtNHKEtfXnNPyExeSWV2IHdy7zFwepBvsBpcLwcLFTloLYA9yFZXV2d01AZba3qLbWzANlqrcFCANsTGhCq5NQ6k3ANIAFmbXgdsQakQg273g2gkDYnLVPOVmJ44x_wqD5rqUG5Vdlfm-yz0UahOqG5ZlvpCXKYUMq0f61p3nqLnCcd5FS6jT4PQJ6FM2QDA_mCMcZuU1kKZ-bMHoU__37t_Qplj9-f0faomN9yXlHOaTSsaeblhypsW_7bOh1NfAQAA___toIXB)** Big companies charge THOUSANDS for hearing aids--but guess what? Hey, it's Chris.
**Election Day is in 29 days, and the New Hampshire Senate race is closer than ever.**
John Sununu's backers -- Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and the Republican establishment and their network of special interest donors -- are pouring over $50 million to try and buy this seat.
**To compete with their millions, we need you in this fight with us.**
**[Can you chip in $10 today to keep New Hampshire blue in this Toss Up race?](https://substack.com/redirect/16785726-f537-4309-8894-14f1e17f8276?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/16785726-f537-4309-8894-14f1e17f8276?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
On Friday I joined fired-up Granite Staters in Rochester for a rally alongside Pete Buttigieg, Cinde Warmington, Stefany Shaheen, and honored guests to talk about what's at stake in this election and the work ahead.
I'm grateful to everyone who came out and spent their Friday night with us.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/16785726-f537-4309-8894-14f1e17f8276?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
