Photo by Ahmad Al-Basha / AFP via Getty Images. Monday, October 5, 2026 -** Yemen : Yemen's Saudi-backed government announces operation to retake Sana'a. Saudi-led coalition deploys 100 warplanes as Yemeni forces launch offensive. U.S. gives Saudi Arabia over 200 Ansarallah targets but holds off on direct strikes. Aramco CEO says rebuilding global oil stocks could take two years. Iran : U.S. bombers withdrawn from UK's Royal Air Force Fairford base. Middle East crude exports surpass pre-Iran war levels. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps orders tanker to turn back in Strait of Hormuz after string of attacks. Iran summons Norwegian ambassador over Starlink operations. Iraq to resume direct flights to Iran on Thursday. Palestine: Israeli attacks kill 15 across Gaza since Saturday. Israeli forces kill worker, settlers attack olive harvesters across the occupied West Bank. Palestinian olive sector loses over $157 million since 2023. Israeli attacks damage or destroy 82% of Gaza's buildings. Somalia's president says country won't accept Israeli presence "under any circumstances." Lebanon: Israel launches air and artillery attacks across south Lebanon despite ceasefire. U.S.: President Donald Trump announces $90 payments to 20 million seniors from Medicare Improvement Fund, surprising Congress. War Secretary Pete Hegseth signals some U.S. troops could shift from Europe to Western Hemisphere. Montana court blocks birthdate requirement on absentee ballots that led to thousands of rejections. Judge blocks Department of Homeland Security environmental waivers, slowing border wall construction in Big Bend region. DHS bought five planes from firm of donor to former Secretary Kristi Noem at inflated prices in her final hours as secretary. U.S.-Russia Ukraine talks now include multibillion-dollar Lukoil oil deal tied to Trump allies. OpenAI head Sam Altman says "world should accept some bad things happening" to help AI industry. Trump threatens to "double" costs if South Korea doesn't sign on to Alaska LNG project. Trump posts Sen. Tom Cotton's personal cell number to pressure him on daylight saving time. California woman arrested for allegedly spying on Taiwanese president's son for China. International: U.S. strike on boat in Caribbean kills four. Pro-government forces seize capital of Ethiopia's Tigray region. Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia, Sudan leaders issue joint declaration on Ethiopia conflict. Arrested journalists in Egypt describe torture, forced confessions. Flavio Bolsonaro outperforms presidential polls, will face current President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Brazil runoff. Pro-Imran Khan march launches after talks with Pakistani government collapse. India, Pakistan summon each other's diplomats over deadly border incident. Mass protests demanding election chief's resignation enter third day across India. Air strike kills UN aid truck driver in Sudan's South Kordofan, World Food Program says; Rapid Support Forces accused of seizing WFP aid trucks. Nationalist party of Serb politician Milorad Dodik claims victory in Bosnia election despite his ban from office. Nicaragua withdraws from Central American Parliament. Russia strikes Kyiv bridge as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz makes unannounced visit. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukraine is ready for U.S.-backed trilateral talks, accuses Russia of sharing jet technology with North Korea. Japan summons U.S. ambassador after Marine arrested in Okinawa murder. Philippines accuses Chinese maritime forces of obstructing anti-blast-fishing operation near Thitu Island. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Yemen Yemen 's Saudi-backed government announces operation to retake Sana'a: Rashad al-Alimi, head of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, Monday the launch of a military and security operation dubbed "Dawn of Yemen," aimed at retaking the capital Sana'a from Ansarallah and restoring control over state institutions. "The Dawn of Yemen operation has begun to restore state institutions, liberate the capital Sana'a, and end the Houthi coup," Al-Alimi said, a day after announcing the start of military operations to "restore the remaining territory of the Republic and extend state authority nationwide." Mohammed Al-Bukhaiti, a member of Ansarallah's political bureau, Al-Alimi's announcement, saying "the war today is between Yemen and Saudi Arabia." He said Saudi aircraft were bombing Yemen while Ansarallah forces were responding "with missiles and drones deep inside Saudi territory," adding that "it is the Saudi regime that controls the mercenary forces, not Rashad al-Alimi." Saudi-led coalition deploys 100 warplanes as Yemeni forces launch offensive: The Saudi-led coalition said Monday that 100 fighter jets were taking part in "Operation Dawn of Yemen," providing round-the-clock air support to Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and air cover over the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. Coalition spokesperson claimed 324 "high-value" targets had been destroyed since the operation began. The coalition's intervention follows overnight Saudi-backed strikes on Sana'a and the northern province of Saada. On the ground, Saudi-backed forces claimed Monday to have taken large parts of Dhubab district overlooking Bab al-Mandab. They also claimed control of the Dhubab airstrip and key positions around the strait, while Ansarallah-aligned media denied that Saudi-backed forces had advanced. Reuters reported that fighting remained under way in the area. Elsewhere, Saudi-backed forces claimed gains in southern Taiz. The military claimed it had carried out 1,122 attacks across Saada, Al-Jawf, Taiz and the western coast, killing or otherwise "neutralizing" 1,747 Ansarallah fighters. The figures could not be independently verified. Ansarallah said Sunday it had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Aramco facilities in Riyadh and Khurais, causing major fires. It said the strikes were retaliation for 50 Saudi airstrikes and missiles over the previous 12 hours on Sana'a, al-Jawf, Taiz, Amran, Hajjah, and Saada. U.S. gives Saudi Arabia over 200 Ansarallah targets but holds off on direct strikes: The U.S. military Saudi Arabia with intelligence and targeting data for its operations against Ansarallah in Yemen, including more than 200 targets over the past two weeks, a U.S. official told Axios. Washington has twice rejected recent Saudi requests to directly join the fighting. Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman again asked Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday for U.S. airstrikes to support a planned Saudi-backed operation in Yemen, but a U.S. official said Washington "is not going to take kinetic action for now." President Donald Trump also held off on ordering strikes against Ansarallah last week after a request from Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. CENTCOM has raised concerns that direct U.S. involvement in Yemen would divert attention and resources from Iran, according to a U.S. official. U.S. officials said Washington is currently providing Saudi Arabia with support short of direct combat, but direct U.S. military action could still be considered if the Saudi-backed operation runs into difficulties. Aramco CEO says rebuilding global oil stocks could take two years: Replenishing global oil inventories while meeting demand could take "up to two years," as disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz continue amid the war with Iran, Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said Monday. "The world entered the crisis with oil inventories of around 10 billion barrels" and has since "lost nearly 3 billion barrels" of oil supply, Nasser said, adding that roughly half the crude and refined products normally shipped through Hormuz have been lost. "Less than 6 billion barrels of commercial inventories remain, and most of them are practically unavailable." "Emergency reserves may get us through the winter, but they do not solve the supply problem in the long term," Nasser said, warning pressure would continue "until the Strait of Hormuz fully reopens and confidence returns." Aramco is considering additional crude export routes and overseas storage, Nasser said. "If we are asked to provide 12 million barrels per day, we can provide it within days." Iran U.S. bombers withdrawn from RAF Fairford : The U.S. abruptly all U.S. long-range bombers deployed to the RAF Fairford airbase in England and returned them to their U.S. home stations over the weekend. The move, which was not explained, comes days after British authorities arrested several individuals over what the officials have claimed was an Iranian plot targeting the base. Fairford has served as a forward operating location for U.S. Global Strike Command and hosted B-1 bombers used in the war against Iran. Middle East crude exports surpass pre-Iran war levels: Crude exports from the Middle East exceeded pre-war levels on four of the final seven days of September, reaching 19.5 million to 22.5 million barrels per day (bpd), according to provisional data from ship-tracking firm Kpler reported by Reuters via Al Jazeera. Before the U.S.-Israel war on Iran, exports averaged about 18 million bpd. The seven-day average for crude exports stood at 18.5 million bpd on October 1, while combined flows of crude, refined products, chemicals and other non-gas liquids averaged 22.4 million bpd in the seven days through September 30. IRGC commander Ali Fadavi disputed the scale of traffic Sunday, saying only "three to four million barrels" of oil were moving through the route each day and describing that volume as "negligible" compared with pre-war levels. Kpler's figures include Strait of Hormuz transits, Red Sea flows, terminal exports, and ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman, but exclude vessels traveling with their tracking transponders switched off. IRGC orders tanker to turn back in Strait of Hormuz after string of attacks: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps ordered an inbound tanker in the Strait of Hormuz to turn back on Monday, warning that the vessel would otherwise be targeted, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations. The tanker complied with the order, which was issued about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. The incident follows three consecutive days of attacks on tankers in and around the Strait. On Sunday, a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile that damaged its engine room. On Saturday, a crude oil tanker was hit on its port side by an unknown projectile four nautical miles east of Oman. On Friday, another tanker was struck during an outbound transit, causing a small fire and blackout before the vessel resumed its journey. No casualties or environmental impacts were reported in any of the three attacks. Iran summons Norwegian ambassador over Starlink operations: Iran Norway's ambassador in Tehran on Sunday and lodged a formal protest over Oslo's failure to stop unauthorized Starlink operations inside Iran. Iran's Foreign Ministry accused the U.S. and Israel of using Starlink to advance an "interventionist and divisive agenda" in Iran and criticized Norway for taking no effective action despite repeated requests from Tehran. Iraq to resume direct flights to Iran on Thursday: Iraqi Airways will direct flights to Iran on October 8, Iraq's Transport Ministry announced Monday. The new schedule will include daily flights between Najaf International Airport and Tehran, Mashhad and Isfahan. Iraq halted flights to and from Iran on September 25 in line with U.S. sanctions and subsequently sought exemptions for pilgrimage, medical and educational travel. Reuters reported that the U.S. Treasury exemption for Iraqi Airways runs for one month, with a more permanent arrangement potentially to follow. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, five Palestinians were killed--three in new Israeli attacks and two due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and 26 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. One body was also recovered. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,243 killed, with 175,232 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,460 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,116, while 836 bodies have been recovered. 181 Palestinians were added to the cumulative death toll after their data was completed and verified, the Ministry noted. Israeli attacks kill 15 across Gaza since Saturday: One Palestinian was killed and more than five others were wounded, including two children, on Monday in an Israeli drone on the southern Al-Mawasi area west of Khan Younis, according to WAFA. Several Palestinians were wounded, including one critically, when an Israeli drone near the Taiba Towers west of Khan Younis. In northern Gaza, a woman was shot in the head by Israeli naval forces in the Al-Sudaniya area northwest of Gaza City. Another woman was wounded by Israeli quadcopter fire in the Zeitoun neighborhood, southeast of Gaza City. On Saturday, Israeli attacks nine Palestinians, including four women and a child, across Gaza. An Israeli airstrike on the Al-Asala building in western Gaza City killed five people: two Palestinian Christian women, an elderly woman and her daughter, and one man. Five Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks across the Strip on Sunday. Israeli forces kill worker, settlers attack olive harvesters across the occupied West Bank: Hebron: Israeli forces a Palestinian worker and wounded two others, one critically, near the entrance to Bani Naim, southeast of Hebron, on Monday, according to WAFA. Israeli settlers ten workers near Khirbet Huwara, east of Yatta, firing into the air and severely beating several of them. Israeli forces also a 140-square-meter home sheltering two families in Al-Deirat, east of Yatta, along with a water well, tent and sheep pens. Jenin: Three Palestinians were when settlers attacked olive harvesters in the Khirbet Amriha and Al-Makhal areas, southwest of Jenin. A 42-year-old man suffered a broken leg, another man was injured in his left hand, and an elderly man was beaten and pepper-sprayed, the Palestinian Red Crescent said. Ramallah: Settlers harvested olives and damaged trees in Umm Safa and Al-Mazra'a Al-Gharbiya, northwest of Ramallah, with the latter attack taking place under Israeli military protection. Settlers also attacked olive harvesters in Al-Taybeh, east of Ramallah. Israeli forces separately Birzeit University with a military bulldozer, demolished and seized a memorial bearing the names of students killed by Israeli forces, and detained a university security guard. Nablus: Settlers from Palestinian farmland in Beita, south of Nablus. In Burqa, northwest of Nablus, settlers attacked farmers harvesting olives in the Bab Al-Jamea area, prevented them from continuing their work and stole a tractor. Six Palestinian families returned to their homes in Tal, southwest of Nablus, after Israeli forces had forced them to leave the houses for more than two months. Palestinian olive sector loses over $157 million since 2023: Palestinian farmers more than $157 million in olive crops since 2023, while some 286,000 olive trees in the occupied West Bank were damaged between 2023 and the end of September 2026 due to Israeli measures and settler attacks, according to the Palestinian Agriculture Ministry. The ministry said around 100,000 olive trees were damaged in the West Bank in the first nine months of 2026 alone, with crop losses exceeding $67 million. Farmers are currently unable to access roughly 30% of the West Bank's olive-growing land, due to Israeli restrictions, settler attacks, land seizures, and the theft of olive crops. In Gaza, more than 90% of an estimated two million olive trees have been lost since the war began in 2023, alongside extensive destruction of infrastructure supporting the olive sector. Israeli attacks damage or destroy 82% of Gaza 's buildings: Around 201,290 buildings in Gaza, or an estimated 82% of all buildings in the Strip, were damaged by Israeli attacks between October 7, 2023 and June 16, 2026, according to the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics. Of those, 134,422 buildings were completely destroyed and another 13,848 severely damaged. Most of Gaza's roughly 2.1 million residents remain displaced and confined to less than 40% of the Strip due to Israeli access restrictions. Somalia 's president says country won't accept Israeli presence "under any circumstances": Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud Al Jazeera on Sunday that Somalia will not accept an Israeli presence "under any circumstances." In the interview, he alleged that Israel intends to establish a naval base in the port city of Berbera, and to use the city's airport. He called these plans part of a "Greater Israel" project and described Israel as a "destabilizing force" which regularly violates international law. Berbera is within the territory claimed by the self-declared republic of Somaliland, whose statehood Israel became the first to recognize in December 2025. Mogadishu insists Berbera remains part of the Somali Republic. He also told the outlet that the United States remains Somalia's strongest partner against "terrorism." Lebanon Israel launches air and artillery attacks across south Lebanon despite ceasefire: Israeli warplanes strikes on Kfar Tebnit and Wadi Al-Hujair in southern Lebanon on Monday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported, while Israeli forces artillery shelled the outskirts of Hadatha and Bra'shit. Overnight, Israeli shelling also targeted Al-Mansouri and Majdal Zoun. U.S. News Trump announces $90 payments to 20 million seniors from Medicare Improvement Fund, surprising Congress: President Donald Trump announced on Saturday to send $90 payments to more than 20 million Medicare Part B enrollees this month, funded by about $2 billion from the Medicare Improvement Fund, which has gone unused for its stated purpose--namely, improving Medicare's hospital and medical insurance programs--since its 2008 creation. The announcement caught congressional offices in both parties by surprise and could unravel unrelated funding talks, a GOP aide told the Washington Post. Lawmakers originally intended to use Improvement Fund monies to help fund several other programs, including the Community Health Center Fund, the National Health Service Corps, the Teaching Health Center Graduate Medical Education program and several special diabetes programs, according to the aide. Hegseth signals some U.S. troops could shift from Europe to Western Hemisphere : Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth reporters on Saturday that some U.S. military capabilities currently in Europe could be redeployed "either back home to the big, beautiful base that we're going to build ... or to a different posture in the Western Hemisphere," part of the administration's push for "burden sharing" with the U.S.'s European allies and its increasing focus on military activity in the Western Hemisphere. Hegseth cited expanded partnerships with Ecuador, Honduras, Guatemala, and Panama in his remarks on Saturday, crediting "the bold move the president made in Venezuela" in capturing Nicol as Maduro with opening "a whole new suite of options economically and militarily." He also reiterated the U.S. is at "war" with cartels, vowing to "posture and base as necessary" to take the fight to what he called "those ISIS and Al Qaeda of our hemisphere." Montana court blocks birthdate requirement on absentee ballots that led to thousands of rejections : A Montana state court Friday night that HB 719, a 2025 law requiring absentee voters to include their birthdate on ballot envelopes or have their votes rejected, violates the state constitution, a win for disability advocates who argued the requirement increased the risk of valid ballots being thrown out over technicalities. The law led to nearly 3,000 rejected mail ballots in the November 2025 election in a state where roughly 80 percent of voters cast absentee ballots. State officials failed to produce evidence of voter fraud justifying the law or explain how the birthdate requirement would prevent it, the court noted in its decision, stressing as well "the undisputed fact HB 719 has resulted in thousands of ballots being rejected due to a missing or incorrect birth year." Judge blocks DHS environmental waivers, slowing border wall construction in Big Bend region : U.S. District Judge Kathleen Cardone a preliminary injunction Friday blocking the Department of Homeland Security from using waivers that exempted border barrier construction from historical and environmental protection laws across more than 500 miles of Texas's Big Bend region, which includes Big Bend Ranch State Park and Big Bend National Park. The order requires DHS to follow those laws while the legal challenge brought by Friends of the Ruidosa Church, river guide Danny William Miller and the Center for Biological Diversity proceeds. The ruling follows a separate judge's Thursday denial of a temporary restraining order specific to the national park, where the administration paused work through Sept. 30. DHS has said it is considering reducing the project's scope, for which a $1.7 billion contract was already doled out to construct a "Big Bend border wall." In filings, the administration said it would announce a final decision this week. DHS bought five planes from Noem donor 's firm at inflated prices in her final hours as secretary: On Kristi Noem 's last day as homeland security secretary, DHS to pay Daedalus Aviation Corporation $108 million for a luxury 737 that the firm had bought months earlier from a seller asking under $90 million, plus $106 million for two Gulfstream jets Daedalus had purchased for about $83 million and $45 million each for two 17-year-old 737 passenger jets that six aviation experts told the Times were worth roughly $15-30 million, according to a Sunday report from the New York Times. Daedalus's chairman, William Walters , gave $10,000 to Noem's political action committee in 2024, and his companies received more than $900 million in DHS contracts under Noem. Her successor at DHS, current secretary Markwayne Mullin , explored canceling the deal but, per two White House officials, was advised by Chief of Staff Susie Wiles against it over potential financial penalties. U.S.-Russia Ukraine talks now include multibillion-dollar Lukoil oil deal tied to Trump allies : U.S.-Russia negotiations over ending the Ukraine war have to include a multibillion-dollar sale of Lukoil's international oil assets, the New York Times reported on Saturday, with the leading bidder group featuring Todd Boehly --a Trump donor who gave $2 million to Trump-aligned causes--alongside Qatar's Khayyat brothers , who have business ties with Jared Kushner andIvanka Trump , an Abu Dhabi fund controlled by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed that is also a business partner of Kushner and bought a large stake in Trump's World Liberty Financial, and the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation. Putin first raised the deal with Steve Witkoff and Kushner at a Sept. 5 Kremlin meeting, and U.S. approval would lift sanctions on the assets, instantly boosting their value. The deal awaits approval from the Treasury Department, with the current extension of sanctions relief on Lukoil's U.S. businesses running through Oct. 29. Altman says "world should accept some bad things happening" to help AI industry: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman his firm's worldview with that of rival firm Anthropic in an interview with POLITICO's Decoded, saying "we believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency." He rejected Anthropic's calls for centralization and regulation in the industry, calling this "a completely unacceptable trade-off." The comments come as the two companies' policy positions have converged in recent months, with Altman backing Dario Amodei 's call to slow development of the most advanced models, OpenAI endorsing stricter state safety laws and lobbyists for OpenAI backing a bipartisan House proposal requiring outside safety evaluators. Trump threatens to "double" costs if South Korea doesn't sign on to Alaska LNG project: President Trump he "didn't jump the gun" in announcing South Korean participation in a $50 billion Alaska LNG project. "Tell them if they don't sign shortly, I'm going to double it up," Trump said Friday, without specifying what would be doubled. Seoul has said it is still assessing the project, with participation dependent on commercial viability and compliance with domestic legal procedures. Trump posts Sen. Tom Cotton 's personal cell number to pressure him on daylight saving time: President Trump the personal cellphone number of Sen. Tom Cotton (R-Ark.), chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, on Saturday and urged Arkansans to call and tell him to "GET IT DONE" on the Sunshine Protection Act, a bill to make daylight saving time permanent that passed the House in July but faces Senate opposition from Cotton and other Republicans. California woman arrested for allegedly spying on Taiwanese president 's son for China: The FBI Wanying Zhang , 34, of Irvine, California, at Los Angeles International Airport on Sunday before her planned departure to China, charging her with acting as an unregistered foreign agent for allegedly surveilling a son of Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te at the direction of Chinese officials. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News U.S. strike on boat in Caribbean kills four: The U.S. military it attacked a suspected drug-smuggling boat in the Caribbean on Sunday, killing four people. U.S. Southern Command said the boat, a go-fast vessel, was targeted along known smuggling routes, but the military provided no evidence it was carrying drugs; a video posted on X appeared to show an explosion destroying the moving boat. Sunday's attack brings the total killed in boat strikes to at least since the Trump administration began targeting alleged "narcoterrorists" in September 2025. Flavio Bolsonaro outperforms polls, will face Lula in Brazil runoff: Brazilian Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro about 47 percent of valid votes in Brazil's first-round presidential election Sunday, exceeding his performance in private polls conducted before the election and narrowly outpacing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who won 44.9 percent of the vote. The two are set to face each other in an Oct. 25 runoff. Pro-government forces seize capital of Ethiopia 's Tigray region: Pro-government forces, led by the Tigray Peace Forces (TPLF) militia, in a Sunday Facebook post that they had regained control of Mekelle, the capital of Ethiopia's Tigray region, with a source close to the militia saying fighters entered the city center Saturday afternoon, followed by the Ethiopian military. The TPLF confirmed it had retreated and said the regional government would be "temporarily moved out of Mekelle and operate from somewhere else." The loss of Mekelle is a major setback for the anti-government coalition led by the TPLF, which announced its offensive against Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government on September 23. Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia, Sudan leaders issue joint declaration on Ethiopia conflict: The leaders of the Egyptian, Eritrean, Somali and Sudanese governments--Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Isaias Afwerki, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Abdel Fattah al-Burhan-- a joint declaration regarding clashes in Ethiopia on Sunday after a meeting in New Alamein City, Egypt. The resolution appears to target several Ethiopian policies: it states that Red Sea control should remain with coastal states, a response to landlocked Ethiopia's pursuit of sea access, and warns against "unilateral measures" harming downstream states over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam. The declaration also backed Sudan's military-led government and urged a Sudanese-led political process. Ethiopia has accused Egypt, Eritrea, and Sudan of backing the TPLF-led armed alliance fighting its government--claims all three deny. Arrested journalists in Egypt describe torture, forced confessions: Several of the journalists from the news platform Matsdaash who were detained and forcibly disappeared in Egypt last week told prosecutors on Sunday they had been tortured at National Security Agency facilities in the days following their arrests, to the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR). The journalists described being bound with their hands behind their backs and blindfolded while being held and interrogated at National Security facilities. They also reported beatings, forced stripping, electric shocks, and threats to harm them or their families, EIPR reported. The journalists also said officers forced them to read statements on camera in order to record false confessions. The prosecution's questioning of five of the journalists--Abdallah Qadry, Islam Barakat, Omar Helal, Mohamed Adel, and Mohamed Mahmoud--is scheduled to continue on Monday. Questioning was completed on Sunday for the sixth journalist, Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emeira, and the Supreme State Security Prosecution ordered him to be held in pretrial detention for 15 days pending investigation. The families and lawyers of the journalists still do not know where they are being held. On Capitol Hill, several members of congress have called for the journalists' immediate release, including the , co-chaired by Reps. Don Beyer and Suzan DelBene; of Michigan, of Vermont, of Maryland, and of Oregon. Pro-Imran Khan march launches after talks with government collapse: More than 5,000 supporters of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan a protest march Sunday from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province toward Islamabad after two rounds of scheduled talks between the PTI and the government over the weekend failed to reach a resolution. The march was originally planned for Sept. 27 and aims to secure the release of former Prime Minister Imran Khan and his three sisters. It is set to reach Khairabad, 80 km from the capital, by Thursday, where the PTI will announce its "next phase." Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi accused KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi of "sabotaging" negotiations and warned authorities would "pursue [protesters] one by one" for violating an Islamabad High Court order barring parties from occupying public roads. The Pakistani government has also blocked main routes into the capital using shipping containers. India, Pakistan summon each other 's diplomats over deadly border incident: India and Pakistan each other's top diplomats Saturday over an October 2 incident in which Pakistan says India's Border Security Force used "unprovoked lethal force" to kill two unarmed Pakistani civilians in the Bedian sector of their international border. In its account of the incident, India claimed three people crossed illegally into Punjab's Ferozepur sector and kept moving toward the border fence despite repeated warnings, forcing the BSF to "engage them for posing an imminent security threat." Pakistan has demanded an "immediate, transparent and credible investigation" into the incident. India dismissed Pakistan's account of the killings as "baseless and motivated," describing the incident as part of "a clear pattern of repeated cross-border movement by armed narcotics syndicates operating from Pakistan." Mass protests demanding election chief 's resignation enter third day across India: Thousands of youth and opposition protesters for a third straight day Sunday, demanding the resignation of Election Commission of India chief Gyanesh Kumar over voter-roll revisions critics say have removed millions of voters in ways benefiting Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party. Opposition leaders Raj and Uddhav Thackeray led a large protest march in Mumbai on Sunday. Similar demonstrations continued in New Delhi on Sunday evening, where police have detained dozens and filed cases against some for violating bans on mass gatherings. An opposition alliance plans to march to the election commission's office Tuesday, while the Cockroach Janta Party, a major force in these protests, plans to hold a major rally in New Delhi on October 10. Air strike kills UN aid truck driver in Sudan 's South Kordofan, WFP says; RSF accused of seizing WFP aid trucks: An air strike on clearly marked World Food Program trucks carrying food aid a driver Saturday in South Kordofan as the convoy traveled between two army-controlled cities, the WFP said Sunday, without identifying who was responsible. The agency called for an investigation into the killing and said it underscores "the increasingly challenging security environment in Sudan and the risks that aid workers face." Separately on Sunday, Abdel Baqi Mohamed Hamed, humanitarian aid commissioner for the Darfur regional government, the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces of seizing 32 World Food Programme trucks from a 60-truck convoy that crossed from Chad through the Tina border point last week. He said the RSF had released 12 of the 44 trucks it had originally seized, but continues to hold the remainder while demanding large extortion payments. Dodik 's party claims victory in Bosnia election despite his ban from office: Preliminary results from Bosnia and Herzegovina's Sunday general election Zeljka Cvijanovic of banned Bosnian Serb leader Milorad Dodik's right-wing Alliance of Independent Social Democrats (SNSD) party leading the race for the Serb seat in the country's three-member presidency. The victory would reinforce Dodik's influence despite his conviction last year for defying the international envoy overseeing the 1995 peace agreement, which barred him from the ballot. Leftist Denis Becirovic led in the race for the Bosniak seat, and Croat nationalist Darijana Filipovic appears poised to take the seat reserved for her coethnics. Nicaragua withdraws from Central American Parliament: Nicaragua's foreign ministry Saturday that it would immediately withdraw from the Central American Parliament, denouncing the 1987 treaty establishing the six-country body and calling its exit "a full exercise of its sovereignty." The announcement comes a day after the Organization of American States passed a resolution urging Nicaraguan authorities to free political prisoners and restore civil liberties. The move continues a pattern of retreat from international institutions by the government of Daniel Ortega and Rosario Murillo, following Nicaragua's 2023 exit from the OAS, which it called a tool of "U.S. interventionism," and its 2025 announcement of withdrawal from the UN Human Rights Council after a UN report urged action on its rights abuses. Russia strikes Kyiv bridge as Germany 's Merz makes unannounced visit: Russia the Northern Bridge over the Dnipro River in Kyiv on Sunday, the same day German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made an unannounced visit to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. It was the second Kyiv bridge hit this weekend, also damaging a road and hot water supply, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko. Addressing his visit, during which he toured the missile-damaged National Academy of Sciences with Zelenskyy, Merz wrote that "if Russia is not stopped, its war machine will sooner or later turn against us." On Sunday, Germany announced that it would send $1.1 billion in military aid to Ukraine, in addition to $394 million to repair Ukraine's energy sector. The two countries are also set to finalize a deal to jointly produce long-range drones capable of traveling more than 600 miles. Zelenskyy says Ukraine ready for U.S.-backed trilateral talks, accuses Russia of sharing jet technology with North Korea: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at a Kyiv news conference with Merz on Sunday that Ukraine is ready to join trilateral technical-level talks with the U.S. and Russia by the end of October, confirming the UAE, which has hosted prior rounds, could again serve as the venue or "another country proposed by the American side." U.S. mediation efforts had been paused since Washington launched its war on Iran. Zelenskyy also Russia on Sunday of sharing jet-drone technology with North Korea, answering "yes, of course" when asked about the matter, adding "they are sharing with North Korea all the technologies... because North Korea helped them with missiles." Russia has sharply increased its use of jet drones against Ukraine in recent weeks, and Ukraine has so far had no effective countermeasure beyond using combat aircraft. Japan summons U.S. ambassador after Marine arrested in Okinawa murder: Japan U.S. Ambassador George Glass after Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard, a 20-year-old U.S. Marine, was arrested on suspicion of robbing and murdering 39-year-old Anna Yagi in Naha, Okinawa. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi called the incident "extremely brutal and heinous" and said Japan "lodged a strong protest" with the U.S. envoy. Philippines accuses Chinese maritime forces of obstructing anti-blast-fishing operation near Thitu Island: The Philippine Coast Guard on Sunday that Chinese vessels blocked a Philippine law enforcement operation against a foreign fishing vessel suspected of dynamite fishing near Thitu Island (Pag-asa) in the South China Sea, with two China Coast Guard ships sounding horns, radio-challenging, shadowing, and blocking Philippine boats while a Chinese navy helicopter circled the team four times. The suspect vessel then fled toward Chinese-built Subi Reef, and Philippine authorities ended the pursuit for safety reasons. Separately, the Philippine military said a Chinese J-16 fighter jet repeatedly approached and maneuvered close to a Philippine patrol aircraft over Scarborough Shoal on Saturday, creating an aviation safety risk. Hey y'all,
Today is the last day to register to vote. Please check your voter registration status here: [IWillVote.com/TX](https://substack.com/redirect/e3a062a4-789f-44c9-85fb-a58f3b196a6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
We are less than one month away from Election Day and just two short weeks from the start of early voting. Registering to vote is the first step to making your voice heard.
Greg Abbott has had over a decade to make Texas a place where all of us can thrive, but instead, he's put his billionaire donors ahead of everyday Texans. He's allowed property taxes to skyrocket 85% under his tenure. He's robbed our neighborhood schools of over $1 billion with his school voucher scam. And he's sold Texas communities out to big data centers.
This election is our chance to change Texas for the better. We have to ask ourselves, is this the Texas that is by and for the people or is this the billionaire's world and the rest of us just live here?
I know I'm fighting for the version of Texas where we all have a seat at the table and a chance to achieve our version of the American Dream. Realizing this vision for Texas starts with all of us showing up to the polls to vote for our future.
But before we cast our ballots, let's make sure we are registered to vote. Check your voter registration status here: [IWillVote.com/TX](https://substack.com/redirect/e3a062a4-789f-44c9-85fb-a58f3b196a6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We are almost at the finish line.
Gina

name: Jen Kiggans
subject: From Navy helicopter pilot to Congress
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kiggans for Congress
body:
I am about to ask you what I know is no small favor.

| Peter,
**I know your inbox is probably overflowing right now with politicians begging for your hard-earned money using every scare tactic in the book.**
_I truly hate having to send messages like this, but I really appreciate your time!_
My last message didn't get the response I was hoping for, and now I'm starting to feel like we're falling behind. We can't keep fighting if we don't have the resources to keep the lights on and pay my amazing staff.
Let me take a second to re-introduce myself: _**My name is Jen Kiggans.**_
I am a former Navy helicopter pilot. I flew H-46s and H-3s in the Persian Gulf. After my time in the military, I used my GI Bill benefits to go back to school and become a board-certified Geriatric Nurse Practitioner. I am married to a retired Navy F/A-18 pilot, and now I am a proud Navy Mom.
---
[](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.)
---
And that is exactly __**WHY**__ I ran for Congress in 2022.
I knew that I needed to step up and do my part to make sure that my four kids inherit a GREAT America!
Against all odds, we flipped Virginia's 2nd District **RED** in one of the tightest, must-win races in the entire country. But elections have serious consequences and these radical Left Democrats are not going to give up without a fight.
Now, National Democrats and Left-leaning Super PACs are raking in millions to attack me and take back the House this year. They want to turn our great commonwealth into California AND my far-Left opponent announced she raised over $1.6 MILLION in the last quarter alone.
_They will stop at absolutely nothing to win._
So today, I’m recruiting YOU to join my mission to save our country from the Democrats' grasp once and for all. That is why I am about to ask you what I know is no small favor. **[Will you chip in just a few dollars to support a former Navy pilot on this critical mission to SAVE OUR GOP HOUSE MAJORITY?](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.)**
---
| [ JOIN JEN’S MISSION >>](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._xS6plf6eMmvcPNe_6BzA)
---
| [CHIP IN RIGHT NOW!](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._iw)
---
As a Navy Vet, I've never turned away from a tough fight, and trust me, I won't start now. But to keep our House Majority intact and continue fighting for our country’s future, I really need your support!
Thank you all so very, very much!
\- Jen Kiggans

---
[](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._UFgbUMgsTwHKZ6V0IA)
---
I would not be where I am today without the help of my incredible and faithful supporters like you. Because of your support, I can keep fighting to make our country stronger.

Together we will get our country back on the right track and secure America’s success!
---

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. Almost closing time, Peter. It’s October, the last full month before Election Day. We have just 29 days to raise the resources we need to beat Mike Lawler. We’ve set some very ambitious goals for this final month, and we have to hit them if we are going to win. There is no room for error in a district as competitive as NY-17. The reality is that Mike Lawler has more money than we do. Lots. And he’s using it to try and bury us with TV ads.
We’ve managed to close the gap with him significantly, thanks to this grassroots team. And brand new polling shows us with a slim lead. But NY-17 is on track to be the most expensive and competitive race in the country. We can’t afford to take our foot off the gas for a moment.
We are going to be outspent. We do not need to match Republicans dollar-for-dollar, but our team needs to be able to field on-the-ground volunteers and push back against their TV ads.
I come from a blue-collar family. After West Point, I spent 16 years in the Army, I did six tours overseas, and was the Director for Counterterrorism at the White House.
Asking for money doesn't come naturally to me. But I have to, if we’re going to meet these October goals.

clean_body: | | | Army veteran Cait Conley is running for Congress in NY-17, one of the most competitive and expensive House districts in the country. These emails are a fundamental part of our campaign's fundraising and organizing efforts, but if you would like to unsubscribe, Almost closing time, Peter. It’s October, the last full month before Election Day. We have just 29 days to raise the resources we need to beat Mike Lawler. We’ve set some very ambitious goals for this final month, and we have to hit them if we are going to win. There is no room for error in a district as competitive as NY-17. If you’re ready to help us win and take back the House for Democrats, you can click right here: | The reality is that Mike Lawler has more money than we do. Lots. And he’s using it to try and bury us with TV ads. We’ve managed to close the gap with him significantly, thanks to this grassroots team. And brand new polling shows us with a slim lead. But NY-17 is on track to be the most expensive and competitive race in the country. We can’t afford to take our foot off the gas for a moment. We are going to be outspent. We do not need to match Republicans dollar-for-dollar, but our team needs to be able to field on-the-ground volunteers and push back against their TV ads. I come from a blue-collar family. After West Point, I spent 16 years in the Army, I did six tours overseas, and was the Director for Counterterrorism at the White House. Asking for money doesn't come naturally to me. But I have to, if we’re going to meet these October goals. This is a grassroots campaign – a huge amount of our budget every month comes from donations of just $10, $5, even $1. So when you see me and my team out there, please know: We’re only able to do so because of the response to emails like this one. | | Dear Peter,

Believe it or not, Election Day is less than a month away — and today, my re-election campaign for Nevada Controller is kicking things up into another gear.

**_We just launched a new phase of our direct voter-contact efforts with another brand-new TV ad — and I wanted you to be among the very first people to get to watch it!_**

Just click the image below to check it out ...
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/o9vsyT9xqO5?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)
---
| Like my first ad, this one highlights my first-term successes in making Nevada’s government more transparent and accountable. But this new ad also includes one of my critical agenda items for a second term: the creation of a new Office of Inspector General, empowered to conduct independent, forensic audits of any entity that receives state funds, in order to ensure _your_ tax dollars aren’t being wasted.

Here’s my ask of you today: I’m hoping you’ll consider [making a contribution](https://us.list-manage.com/5SlGACk3S2S?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) to help us put this new ad directly in front of the voters we need to reach in the closing weeks of this race.

[You can contribute by clicking here](https://us.list-manage.com/tWNrv84ZciW?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73), or, if you prefer, you can contribute by check made out to “Andy For Nevada” and mailed to:

Andy For Nevada
P.O. Box 35666
Las Vegas, NV 89133

Back to my Inspector General bill for a moment. As you may recall, I introduced a bill to create an IG office during the 2025 legislative session. We had a great hearing on the bill, but Democrats ultimately blocked it. Since then, we’ve seen what can happen when a state doesn’t have the proper oversight in place to safeguard tax dollars. The fraud and scandals that have rocked Minnesota — _which also does not have an Inspector General_ — should serve as a huge wake-up call for all of us. Nevada needs to pass this bill to make sure the same thing doesn’t happen here.

**__That’s why I’ve promised to bring my IG bill back in the 2027 session!__**

But first, I need to win. And I’m hoping you can [pitch in a contribution today](https://us.list-manage.com/151GUNJfA2j?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) to make sure I do.

Thank you so much for your commitment to our shared principles, my friend. I’m so grateful for your continued support!

For Nevada’s future,

Andy

clean_body: | | | | Look at this: = In June, the New York Times/Siena poll had me trailing Greg Abbott by 7 points, 51% to 44%. Today, that same poll has me ahead, 49% to 46%. = = Ten-to-one. Dollar for dollar, she's running the best statewide campaign we've ever seen." That's what grassroots supporters like you have built $5 and $10 at a time. We haven't come close to matching Abbott's money, but every dollar has gone further than anyone thought it could. = The Times was also honest about what still stands in our way. Texas has 20 separate media markets, and national donors routinely pass the state over because reaching all of them is so expensive. And one in five Texas voters still doesn't know who I am. Here's what the last three months have taught us: the more Texans get to know me, the more this race moves. Every one of those voters is someone we can reach, but only if we have the resources to do it. Abbott has raised more than $106 million in this race, and he's going to keep spending it in the final month to drag this race back his way. We are 30 days from Election Day. The polls tell us this race can be won. Peter,
I’m writing to ask you to chip in $15 to help Hakeem Jeffries and House Democrats win back the majority. Please let me tell you why I think this moment is different, and why your support here matters so much.
Winning the House isn’t just the top priority for Democrats right now. It’s the most direct path to restoring some basic accountability in Washington, and to proving that the chaos of the last few years isn’t some kind of permanent new normal.
I’ve spent a lot of time reflecting on what really makes America great. It’s not that we’ve always gotten it right. It’s that we’ve built a system of governance around the idea that leaders must be accountable to the people – not the other way around. It’s our revolutionary promise of political equality, economic opportunity, and personal liberty.
That’s what’s on the line.
This election asks something of us. It asks whether we’re willing to do the work of making change, not just express outrage at the way things are. And I believe we are ready.
Helping Hakeem Jeffries bring back a Democratic House majority is one of the most important things we can all do. What they need is the resources to compete – and that’s where you come in.

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

body:
You’re invited to tonight’s Take Back The House virtual phone bank with Team Tran and special guests!

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/derektranforcongress/2026-oct-5-phone-bank-blast-6433068?e=fa48019594)

| | Dear Supporter,
You’re invited to tonight’s _**Take Back The House**_ virtual phone bank with Team Tran and special guests!
**WHEN:** Monday, October 5 5:30 - 7:30 p.m. PST**WHERE:** Virtual**RSVP:**[**HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/pQF1OjumSC7?e=fa48019594&c2id=2d2f4814b3c86de5c7569386ec1a86b4)
To receive your virtual meeting link, phone bank training, and hear from special guests, please RSVP via the link above. I hope to see you there!
Sincerely,Congressman Derek Tran
---
| | ###
_The son of refugees who worked hard and sacrificed for the American Dream, Congressman Derek Tran joined the Army at 18 to give back to the country that has given him so much. Wanting to continue his career in public service, he ran in California's 45th district to put people ahead of politics and protect democracy, and won. Now, he's running again to ensure everyone no matter what neighborhood they come from has the opportunity to succeed without fear of their freedoms being taken away._
_California’s 45th Congressional District remains one of the most contested battleground races in the country. Last cycle, Derek Tran flipped the seat by just over 600 votes (a 0.2% margin) in the second-closest and most expensive House race ($46 million spent) in the country. A majority-minority district, the District has the third largest AAPI population (41%) of any Congressional District, is 28% Latino, and is home to the largest Vietnamese community in the country. Following Proposition 50, this district brings in over 15,000 new Hispanic voters and over 7,000 new Vietnamese voters, and has a DPI of 52.8%. It includes all or part of the cities of Garden Grove, Westminster, Fountain Valley, Cerritos, Buena Park, Placentia, Hawaiian Gardens, Cypress, Artesia, Los Alamitos, La Palma, Norwalk, Stanton, Lakewood, Santa Ana, Seal Beach, and Fullerton, as well as the unincorporated community of Midway City._

clean_body: A man that loyal to the indefensible is unfit to represent you. | | Peter, You can learn everything about a politician from the company they keep and the people they vouch for. By that measure, Keith Self has told us who he is over and over. He endorsed Pete Hegseth, a likely war criminal, and stands by him through every disgrace. | Then he threw his weight behind Bo French for Railroad Commissioner, a man whose antisemitic remarks were ugly enough that Karl Rove, of all people, refused to support him. | Think about how hateful you have to be for the architect of the modern GOP attack machine to sour on you. This proves once again that in Keith Self we are not dealing with a conservative but a fanatic. Keith Self is a bigot and a bully who endorses other bigots and bullies. His own hometown sees it. McKinney Councilman Justin Beller just called him "unfit to serve our community" and endorsed this campaign because Self tried to tear his own hometown apart over a legally approved mosque. But let 's set the ugliness aside for a moment and ask a practical question. What has all that hate gotten you? Your gas prices went up. Your grocery bill went up. Your overtime protections died without a word from Self. He has not held a town hall or passed a thing this district can point to. We pay this man $174,000 a year, and his entire output is a recall petition against his own neighbors and a string of endorsements for bigots like Bo French. Hate and bluster is not a record. It never has been. This movement is building the opposite. From packed town halls where every question gets answered, to volunteers who show up when a neighbor needs a hand, service comes first here. And to prove it, last week I joined my fellowTake BAC candidates in Washington for an Accountability Summit where grassroots Democrats from across the country committed to two promises: | We will hold this administration accountable for its crimes. And we will hold our own party accountable to the people it serves. That is the choice on the ballot in less than 30 days. Two years of service and solutions. Or two more years of spite and stunts. **Our theory:** a big miner that needs to replace its reserves has two choices. Spend a decade exploring with no guarantee, or buy a company that already has proven ounces in the ground. Central banks bought a record 289 tonnes of gold in the second quarter of 2026, and kept buying even as prices dipped. Gold traded above $5,300 in January and has stayed above $4,000 since. Follow the money | | The Takeover Wave Is Already Here ---|--- | Agnico Eagle → Rupert Resources$2.12 billion · April 2026Part of a push to consolidate Finland’s Central Lapland Greenstone Belt, with Aurion Resources (~$351M) and a $325M stake from B2Gold. | Equinox Gold + Orla Mining~$5.1 billion · May 2026Creates an $18.5 billion North American producer targeting 1.1 million ounces a year. | Newmont → Barrick (Nevada JV)$1.95 billion cashNewmont pays to expand the joint venture’s assets. What it means Our theory: a big miner that needs to replace its reserves has two choices. Spend a decade exploring with no guarantee, or buy a company that already has proven ounces in the ground. At $4,000-plus gold, it can afford to pay whatever premium it takes. That turns the best-positioned juniors into takeover targets, and their shareholders into the sellers. The first in line for a premium bid. | | WATCH The majors Rich in cash but short on reserves. Forced to pay up to stay the same size. | | LOSING Explorers without results In a market that rewards proven ounces, hope alone doesn’t get bought. | ClassificationConfirmation Record gold prices, record central-bank buying, shrinking reserves and almost no new discoveries. The majors have only one way to stay big: buy. This phase of a gold bull market historically rewards whoever owns the targets before the bids arrive. | The riddle · answer at the end of the fileGold is near record highs and the biggest miners are flush with cash. Why would the biggest winners of this bull market be small companies? | Riddle answer Because the giants need what the small companies own. A major can’t print new ounces. It has to buy them, and in a takeover the premium goes to the shareholders of the company being bought. An Israeli soldier stands guard as young men gathered during a demonstration by Ultra-Orthodox Jews against Israel's military draft on June 17, 2026 outside the Beit Lid military base in Kfar Yona, Israel. Photo by Amir Levy/Getty Images.
_This article is being co-published with[Capital & Empire](https://substack.com/redirect/4eac0bcd-688c-400d-b42d-1323b7176dbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)._
Israel is at risk of civil war or state collapse, a classified CIA assessment warns, as years of genocide in Gaza and war in Lebanon and Iran deepen political, economic, and social fractures within the country.
The August report, titled "Fracture From Within," was compiled by experts in the CIA's Red Cell, according to two U.S. sources who described the contents of the report to Drop Site News. The Red Cell, which is the unit responsible for providing "alternative analysis" within the agency, produced the assessment through a combination of open source information and U.S. intelligence. The CIA did not respond to a request for comment.
CIA experts pointed to a volatile mix of pressures converging ahead of Israel's elections on October 27: economic crisis and soaring military spending; heavily armed veterans returning from prolonged combat, many carrying serious psychological trauma; growing fury over ultra-Orthodox men who are exempt from military service; escalating settler violence in the occupied West Bank; and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu fighting to hold onto power and igniting a constitutional crisis.
The CIA's "red teams" are tasked with developing analysis and ideas that challenge prevailing assumptions and expose groupthink or blind spots that can take hold within the intelligence apparatus. "The writers of this are Israel experts," a source in the intelligence community noted, "this isn't a fantastical what if--with the upcoming election and the fissures in Israel we should take seriously their conclusion that Israel is one spark away from real internal conflict."
One of the deepest fractures in Israeli politics has emerged not over opposition to the country's war crimes--but over who is expected to fight and who is exempt. Ultra-Orthodox men have historically received broad exemptions from military service while continuing to receive state benefits, an arrangement that has become increasingly contentious amid repeated reserve mobilizations. Their collective refusal to serve is not rooted in opposition to Israel's wars, as ultra-Orthodox leaders argue that military service threatens religious life and their obligation to Torah study. But after years in which reservists have been repeatedly called away from their jobs and families, the [exemption](https://substack.com/redirect/6eee9751-81ad-463e-a025-4b2b0b394af1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has become a potent source of resentment in Israeli society. Households have also been absorbing the costs of Israel's belligerent policies. Food prices have reached [record highs](https://substack.com/redirect/d42a7a29-31de-479d-a3ad-eb044195be9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with the cost of food--including fresh fruit and vegetables--rising 9.5 percent over the past two years, deepening an already severe cost-of-living crisis after years of war.
Yet much of the opposition to Netanyahu is not opposition to Israel's brutality against Palestinians, but anger over how he has managed it. The major anti-Netanyahu Zionist parties are themselves divided over leadership and coalition strategy, while a central line of attack against Netanyahu has been his responsibility for the October 7 security failure. Recent [polling](https://substack.com/redirect/65ab0749-79ad-4362-94d4-b8a597c1a0fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has shown both the Netanyahu and anti-Netanyahu blocs struggling to reach the 61 seats required to govern.
The sources warned that the combination of political fracture and a growing population of heavily armed, traumatized veterans has historical precedents. "Famously the Freikorps of Germany were PTSD-addled veterans with weapons and bloodthirst," he said. "I'm not saying Israel post Gaza is Germany post-WWI but there are certainly aspects of this that ring similar to me."
Israel is also confronting growing isolation abroad, including an erosion of support in the United States that Israeli officials themselves have privately treated as a long-term threat. The August report pointed to Israel increasingly becoming a pariah state as a factor that could lead to state breakdown.
According to another CIA assessment Capital & Empire [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/0a4e3db7-1851-4345-b2c3-37acd68f6bda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in July, Israeli officials believe the American political consensus underpinning the alliance is breaking down and that continued reliance on billions of dollars in direct U.S. military aid may eventually become politically untenable. Their response has been to seek deeper integration into the American military, intelligence, and defense establishment--ties that would be harder for future governments to unwind. By this spring, 60% of Americans viewed Israel unfavorably, up from 53% a year earlier, according to a Pew Research Center [survey](https://substack.com/redirect/13af2ebb-7554-4c5b-89c8-9e0071abbeeb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
That deterioration of support is increasingly visible inside the U.S. national security establishment, as well. "The intelligence community, like America, like the military, like everywhere, is growing frustrated with the real and political capital that's spent on propping up Israel," the source said. "As we're moving forward with further integrating our military-industrial capacity with them, there's deep frustration that we're doing this for a country that dragged us into a war we're losing, a country that spies on us."
The CIA report also tried to game out how these pressures could interact if Israel's internal crisis deepened--how a single spark could turn political fracture into open civil conflict, and what would follow from there. Among the scenarios raised were foreign technology and artificial-intelligence companies pulling investment or personnel from Israel, further eroding an already strained economy, regional governments reconsidering the political and strategic value of deeper normalizing relations with Israel, and Hamas or Hezbollah exploiting a period of domestic weakness. The report specifically used the term "civil conflict," according to the sources.
For decades, Israel's power depended not only on weapons and American backing, but on the projection that its military dominance, intelligence superiority, and internal cohesion made the state effectively unbreakable. But as the assessment warned, beneath that projection of overwhelming force, Israel is accumulating economic, political, and social contradictions that military might alone may not be able to contain.

Israel is at risk of civil war or state collapse, a classified CIA assessment warns, as years of genocide in Gaza and war in Lebanon and Iran deepen political, economic, and social fractures within the country. The August report, titled "Fracture From Within," was compiled by experts in the CIA's Red Cell, according to two U.S. sources who described the contents of the report to Drop Site News. The Red Cell, which is the unit responsible for providing "alternative analysis" within the agency, produced the assessment through a combination of open source information and U.S. intelligence. The CIA did not respond to a request for comment. CIA experts pointed to a volatile mix of pressures converging ahead of Israel's elections on October 27: economic crisis and soaring military spending; heavily armed veterans returning from prolonged combat, many carrying serious psychological trauma; growing fury over ultra-Orthodox men who are exempt from military service; escalating settler violence in the occupied West Bank; and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu fighting to hold onto power and igniting a constitutional crisis. The CIA's "red teams" are tasked with developing analysis and ideas that challenge prevailing assumptions and expose groupthink or blind spots that can take hold within the intelligence apparatus. "The writers of this are Israel experts," a source in the intelligence community noted, "this isn't a fantastical what if--with the upcoming election and the fissures in Israel we should take seriously their conclusion that Israel is one spark away from real internal conflict." One of the deepest fractures in Israeli politics has emerged not over opposition to the country's war crimes--but over who is expected to fight and who is exempt. Ultra-Orthodox men have historically received broad exemptions from military service while continuing to receive state benefits, an arrangement that has become increasingly contentious amid repeated reserve mobilizations. Their collective refusal to serve is not rooted in opposition to Israel's wars, as ultra-Orthodox leaders argue that military service threatens religious life and their obligation to Torah study. But after years in which reservists have been repeatedly called away from their jobs and families, the has become a potent source of resentment in Israeli society. Households have also been absorbing the costs of Israel's belligerent policies. Food prices have reached , with the cost of food--including fresh fruit and vegetables--rising 9.5 percent over the past two years, deepening an already severe cost-of-living crisis after years of war. Yet much of the opposition to Netanyahu is not opposition to Israel's brutality against Palestinians, but anger over how he has managed it. The major anti-Netanyahu Zionist parties are themselves divided over leadership and coalition strategy, while a central line of attack against Netanyahu has been his responsibility for the October 7 security failure. Recent has shown both the Netanyahu and anti-Netanyahu blocs struggling to reach the 61 seats required to govern. The sources warned that the combination of political fracture and a growing population of heavily armed, traumatized veterans has historical precedents. "Famously the Freikorps of Germany were PTSD-addled veterans with weapons and bloodthirst," he said. "I'm not saying Israel post Gaza is Germany post-WWI but there are certainly aspects of this that ring similar to me." Israel is also confronting growing isolation abroad, including an erosion of support in the United States that Israeli officials themselves have privately treated as a long-term threat. The August report pointed to Israel increasingly becoming a pariah state as a factor that could lead to state breakdown. According to another CIA assessment Capital & Empire in July, Israeli officials believe the American political consensus underpinning the alliance is breaking down and that continued reliance on billions of dollars in direct U.S. military aid may eventually become politically untenable. Their response has been to seek deeper integration into the American military, intelligence, and defense establishment--ties that would be harder for future governments to unwind. By this spring, 60% of Americans viewed Israel unfavorably, up from 53% a year earlier, according to a Pew Research Center . That deterioration of support is increasingly visible inside the U.S. national security establishment, as well. "The intelligence community, like America, like the military, like everywhere, is growing frustrated with the real and political capital that's spent on propping up Israel," the source said. "As we're moving forward with further integrating our military-industrial capacity with them, there's deep frustration that we're doing this for a country that dragged us into a war we're losing, a country that spies on us." The CIA report also tried to game out how these pressures could interact if Israel's internal crisis deepened--how a single spark could turn political fracture into open civil conflict, and what would follow from there. Among the scenarios raised were foreign technology and artificial-intelligence companies pulling investment or personnel from Israel, further eroding an already strained economy, regional governments reconsidering the political and strategic value of deeper normalizing relations with Israel, and Hamas or Hezbollah exploiting a period of domestic weakness. The report specifically used the term "civil conflict," according to the sources. For decades, Israel's power depended not only on weapons and American backing, but on the projection that its military dominance, intelligence superiority, and internal cohesion made the state effectively unbreakable. But as the assessment warned, beneath that projection of overwhelming force, Israel is accumulating economic, political, and social contradictions that military might alone may not be able to contain. Enough was enough. Connecticut lawmakers took action to ban dangerous weapons like AR-15’s in their state. Nine other states and D.C. followed suit, banning assault weapons. This was a massive win for public safety. The gun lobby wants to get rid of those bans. What's up, Angry Democrats? Matt here.
Everybody keeps talking about a blue wave. But what would a blue wave actually mean, and what could Democrats realistically do if they won control of both the House and Senate?
For this discussion, I am not going to complicate things with every possible outcome. I am not talking about Democrats winning the House while Republicans keep the Senate. I am also not talking about some massive Democratic supermajority that fundamentally changes the rules.
I am talking about the simplest realistic scenario: Democrats win a narrow majority in the House and at least 51 seats in the Senate.
What happens then?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2e54ae6a-9fa5-48f5-8f4f-497d5d04f9eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
## **First, a Reality Check**
Winning Congress would not mean Democrats could suddenly pass anything they wanted.
Most legislation can still be blocked by the Senate filibuster unless Democrats have 60 votes, use budget reconciliation or change Senate rules. Even if a bill passes both chambers, it would still go to Donald Trump's desk. He could veto it, and overriding that veto would require two-thirds of both the House and Senate.
So let's be honest about what a narrow Democratic majority would mean.
It would be much better at stopping Trump, investigating Trump and slowing down the administration than passing an enormous Democratic legislative agenda.
* * *
## **1\. Block Trump 's Legislative Agenda**
Right now, Republicans control the House, Senate and executive branch. That gives Trump considerable freedom to move legislation through Congress when Republicans remain united.
If Democrats control both chambers, that stops.
Whether Trump wants another artificial-intelligence bill, another round of tax cuts, another funding package or those $5,000 bribery checks, Democrats would control whether that legislation receives a vote and what ultimately reaches his desk.
The same would apply to legislation involving immigration, energy, healthcare, military funding and the federal budget.
Trump could no longer expect Congress to rubber-stamp everything he wants...

| | | Fellow Patriot, Your inbox has been full of deadlines lately. This isn't one of those emails. The end-of-quarter deadline just passed, and I wanted to step off the campaign trail long enough to say it myself: **Thank you!!** When the national Democrats decided Texas was ready to flip, they started pouring millions into this race. They assumed grassroots conservatives would get outspent and give up. You didn't give up, Fellow Patriot. _You helped prove them wrong._ Because of patriots like you, 40,165 people chipped in this quarter - more than we ever imagined would step up to protect our majority. This race is still close for comfort, and it isn't over until Election Day. But I don't take a single contribution for granted. | | | | JoCasta Zamarripa is a lifelong Milwaukeean, a proud daughter of the city’s south side, and a dedicated public servant who’s never stopped fighting for working people. Born and raised in the very neighborhoods she now represents, JoCasta has spent her life pushing for progress that reflects the realities of everyday Wisconsinites.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/xQn8Lj2wKkc?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

She made history as the first Latina and first openly bi member of both the Wisconsin State Legislature and the Milwaukee Common Council. But JoCasta’s leadership is defined by more than her historic firsts—it's grounded in results. She served ten years in the State Assembly and is now in her second term as Alderperson for Milwaukee’s 8th District, where she’s led major efforts on affordable housing, small business licensing reform, and community development.

In 2025, she was the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan, a key step in addressing Milwaukee’s housing crisis by expanding affordable options and preventing displacement. Her approach is practical and persistent—building coalitions, navigating political challenges, and staying rooted in the neighborhoods she serves.

Now, JoCasta is running as a Democrat for Wisconsin Secretary of State to use the platform to fight for what matters: more funding for our schools so families aren’t forced into referenda every election, real housing relief for working people, and affordable child care that lets parents breathe.
