Not $100. Not $50. Not even $25!

Just $15.

Friend, it's Michele Tafoya. I'm sure you've received plenty of political messages this time of year from thankless politicians who have spent the majority of their careers in Washington, lining their own pockets.To be candid with you, that's everything I'm NOT.
I spent the better part of my life on the sidelines watching the best athletes in the world compete at the highest level.
I know what it takes to be a winner, I've seen it firsthand.That's the pedigree I've brought to this campaign.
Not cutting corners, not cheating myself, or letting my team down.
But I can't be the only one bought in if we're going to succeed this fall, Friend.

It's going to take a group of us going the extra mile to create change.

Folks, I'm reaching out with an urgent request.
Adam Hamilton is the Democrat running for U.S. Senate in Kansas, and three polls in a row show him narrowly leading his Republican opponent. We can flip this seat blue.
**That 's why the GOP is panicking. Their top super PAC just launched a MASSIVE ad buy in Kansas to turn the tides against Adam and boost his opponent - and he needs our immediate grassroots support to fight back.**
You've stood by my side while I've faced these kinds of attacks. Now, I'm asking you to show up for Adam. [Will you make a split donation of $10 between my campaign and Adam Hamilton's right now? Flipping this seat - and the Senate - is crucial to getting our country back on the right track.](https://substack.com/redirect/2387658c-8566-40bf-9744-5c65634163d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Adam has been a pastor for the past 36 years, and he's a fifth-generation Kansan.
He's been called to run for Senate for many of the same reasons I have: He loves his home state. He cares deeply about the future of our country. He knows that Washington DC's chaos and corruption are making life harder for folks, and he's ready to fix things.
With experts at RealClearPolitics calling this race a "Toss Up" and the polls continuing to shift in his direction, Adam has what it takes to flip Kansas for the first time in nearly a _century_.
But not without your support - right here, right now. He's getting outspent by the GOP, and he simply cannot fight back without you.**[Will you split $10 to help Adam and me flip our respective seats this November and build a brighter future for all?](https://substack.com/redirect/2387658c-8566-40bf-9744-5c65634163d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thank you.
Roy Cooper

House Minority Leader Jim Durkin wears a mask during the legislative session. (Credit: Justin L. Fowler of The State Journal-Register)
By Jacqueline Garretson, Opinion Contributor

It has been more than five years since COVID-19 changed our lives, but for many Illinois families, the consequences never really went away. Businesses were lost, jobs disappeared, families drained their savings, and children lost something that can never be replaced: their childhood.

Under Gov. JB Pritzker, Illinois families spent 1,155 days under some form of COVID-era emergency declarations, restrictions, and executive orders. For more than three years, Illinoisans lived with a government response that repeatedly changed how we worked, learned, worshiped, and interacted with one another. What was initially presented as a temporary emergency became a prolonged period of government intervention that affected every aspect of daily life.

But the people who paid the greatest price were often those with the least ability to understand what was happening: our children.

In a matter of weeks, their entire world changed. Schools closed. Sports disappeared. Friends became faces on computer screens. Birthday parties, school activities, graduations, and family gatherings were canceled.

Children were isolated during some of the most important developmental years of their lives, and many are still dealing with the consequences. Parents watched their children struggle with anxiety, fear, isolation, and academic setbacks. Years later, many students remain behind where they should be.

Yet instead of confronting those failures honestly, Illinois continues to lower the bar and declare victory.

Changing standards doesn’t change reality. If students are struggling academically, lowering expectations doesn’t make them more successful. It simply makes the numbers look better. Parents in Illinois deserve an education system that tells the truth about where our children are; not one that manipulates the measurements to make politicians look more successful.

And here’s the part voters should not forget: Democrats weren’t the only politicians who supported the COVID response. Some Republicans did too.

Former Illinois House Republican Leader Jim Durkin, along with others in the party, supported restrictions, defended the status quo, and failed to challenge the system, while families and businesses were suffering. Politicians shouldn’t be more concerned with maintaining political relationships than standing up for the people who elected them.

Today, former Illinois House Republican Leader Jim Durkin has endorsed JB Pritzker for Governor. Durkin’s endorsement is a political nod of approval to the very Governor whose COVID policies left such a lasting mark on Illinois families.

To me, that endorsement says a lot. It is a reminder that the old political establishment has never been as divided as the party labels would have us believe.

There was, however, a Republican who was willing to challenge the governor when it mattered: Darren Bailey.

I watched Darren stand on the House floor and tell the political establishment that the path Illinois was taking was wrong. He challenged Pritzker’s restrictions. And while others were willing to go along to get along, Darren was willing to stand up and fight.

You don’t have to agree with Darren Bailey on every issue to recognize the importance of political courage.

Leadership isn’t simply agreeing with the majority when it is politically convenient. Sometimes leadership means standing alone and telling the people in power that they have gone too far.

The next crisis will eventually come. When it does, Illinois families need leaders who understand that government power must have limits and that emergency authority cannot become a blank check.

We need leaders who will listen to parents, protect children, support small businesses, and question the establishment when its power becomes unchecked.

Because those 1,155 days weren’t just numbers on a calendar. They represented birthdays that couldn’t be celebrated, seasons that couldn’t be played, businesses that never reopened, jobs that disappeared, and children who lost years they will never get back.

Five years later, Illinois families are still picking up the pieces. They don’t need politicians to tell them everything worked. They know it didn’t.

They deserve the truth. They deserve accountability. And they deserve leaders who will put people before politics.

That leader is Darren Bailey.

Durkin’s endorsement is a political nod of approval to the very Governor whose COVID policies left such a lasting mark on Illinois families. To me, that endorsement says a lot. It is a reminder that the old political establishment has never been as divided as the party labels would have us believe. There was, however, a Republican who was willing to challenge the governor when it mattered: Darren Bailey. I watched Darren stand on the House floor and tell the political establishment that the path Illinois was taking was wrong. He challenged Pritzker’s restrictions. And while others were willing to go along to get along, Darren was willing to stand up and fight. You don’t have to agree with Darren Bailey on every issue to recognize the importance of political courage. Leadership isn’t simply agreeing with the majority when it is politically convenient. Sometimes leadership means standing alone and telling the people in power that they have gone too far. The next crisis will eventually come. When it does, Illinois families need leaders who understand that government power must have limits and that emergency authority cannot become a blank check. We need leaders who will listen to parents, protect children, support small businesses, and question the establishment when its power becomes unchecked. Because those 1,155 days weren’t just numbers on a calendar. They represented birthdays that couldn’t be celebrated, seasons that couldn’t be played, businesses that never reopened, jobs that disappeared, and children who lost years they will never get back. Five years later, Illinois families are still picking up the pieces. They don’t need politicians to tell them everything worked. They know it didn’t. They deserve the truth. They deserve accountability. And they deserve leaders who will put people before politics. That leader is Darren Bailey. **I’m not some cookie-cutter politician.**
I used to work as a scientist — a geologist, to be specific. After our company was sold and I got laid off, I organized and opened Colorado’s first brewpub, helping revitalize LoDo, a neglected warehouse district in Denver.
I never imagined I’d run for office. I wandered into public service because I felt like our elected officials were mainly making decisions to get re-elected, not solve problems for their constituents. So I ran for mayor, then governor, and eventually senator.
Even though my commute to work got a whole lot longer, my focus hasn’t changed. I’m still deadset on **putting Colorado families first and getting stuff done. And that’s exactly what we’ve done!**
As Denver’s Mayor, we unified the metro area to expand and rejuvenate our public transit. As Governor, we took Colorado from 40th in job creation to the #1 economy in the nation for three straight years. And as your senator, we wrote and passed the largest-ever effort to fight climate change, passed the most consequential housing bill in decades, and lowered drug costs for seniors.
Now I’m running for reelection to finish what we’ve started. We need to help Democrats take back the Senate and bring MAGA’s ruthless agenda to a halt. And we need you on our side.
Unlike other politicians, we don’t take money from corporate PACs. Instead, we rely on grassroots folks like you.
[That’s why I'm depending on your contribution today to help us defend Colorado. Even just $5 here or $10 there goes a long way in a campaign like ours. So we have to ask: will you chip in whatever is meaningful to you today? I used to work as a scientist — a geologist, to be specific. After our company was sold and I got laid off, I organized and opened Colorado’s first brewpub, helping revitalize LoDo, a neglected warehouse district in Denver. I never imagined I’d run for office. I wandered into public service because I felt like our elected officials were mainly making decisions to get re-elected, not solve problems for their constituents. So I ran for mayor, then governor, and eventually senator. Even though my commute to work got a whole lot longer, my focus hasn’t changed. I’m still deadset on putting Colorado families first and getting stuff done. And that’s exactly what we’ve done! As Denver’s Mayor, we unified the metro area to expand and rejuvenate our public transit. As Governor, we took Colorado from 40th in job creation to the #1 economy in the nation for three straight years. And as your senator, we wrote and passed the largest-ever effort to fight climate change, passed the most consequential housing bill in decades, and lowered drug costs for seniors. #### **[Powerful people are counting on us to stop paying attention. We won't. Endless Urgency follows the money, keeps the receipts, and asks the questions people in power would rather see disappear. If you believe corruption deserves scrutiny -- no matter whose name is attached to it -- become a paid subscriber for $8/month and help us keep doing this work.](https://substack.com/redirect/b7387e96-eb26-4483-977a-4748bcaf2fec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

* * *
Last week, a reporter asked me a question I haven't been able to shake.
If Democrats win back the House and the Senate, should they investigate every member of Donald Trump's family? Even Melania? Even Barron?
I could hear what was underneath it. Surely some of them should be off-limits. Surely there's a line. It's the political version of "women and children first" on the Titanic, as if the lifeboats were reserved for the people we feel a little squeamish about scrutinizing.
My answer took about half a second: _Absolutely_. Investigate Melania Trump. Investigate Barron Trump. Investigate all of them.
There are no sacred cows when it comes to the most corrupt family in American history. They have stolen untold sums, tens of billions of dollars. They have turned the presidency into a family business so effectively that every one of them is now basically a billionaire in their own right. Melania and her documentary. Barron and his crypto scams and his relationship with the Tate brothers. It goes on and on. These people have made staggering amounts of money while Donald Trump has held the most powerful office in the world.

And I don't give a shit whether somebody had an official title in the administration. That's not the standard.

If you're the president's wife, his son, his daughter, his son-in-law -- if you have extraordinary access to the President of the United States while simultaneously making enormous amounts of money -- I want to know where that money came from. I want to know who paid it and I want to know what they wanted. All of it should be looked at.
Before anyone accuses me of partisanship, let me be clear: I'm being consistent. I never had a problem with people investigating Hunter Biden and Burisma. If Hunter abused his position to profit off his father's office, I want to know, and I want him held accountable. That's how this is supposed to work.
But let's not pretend the scale is remotely the same. Whatever Hunter Biden did is a hot day in Arizona. What the Trump family has done is the surface of the goddamn sun.
What surprised me was the reaction. All weekend, I heard the same thing: "Come on. Barron's just a kid."
No. He is not a kid. He's a grown-ass man, participating in the adult world and making his own decisions. His best friend is a world-famous human trafficker. And he's involved in the his family's cryptocurrency business. World Liberty Financial isn't some lemonade stand his dad helped him set up. Forbes estimated that the Trump family had already pocketed roughly $780 million from World Liberty by September 2026, with Barron's own fortune estimated at $150 million -- much of it tied to crypto. The venture has also attracted major foreign investment.
And apparently crypto wasn't enough. Barron is also a director of SOLLOS, a privately held yerba mate startup that has raised around $1 million -- because nothing screams "perfectly normal presidential-family business venture" like another Trump company where we have very little visibility into who owns what or what Barron's stake actually is.
So yes, put it _all_ under a microscope.
Barron doesn't get a different set of laws because his father happens to be president. Thinking otherwise is exactly the kind of special treatment that got us here.
I'm sick of watching these people hide behind age, gender, or whatever shield is convenient that week. Melania doesn't get extra protection because she's a woman. If she's complicit in the self-dealing inside this administration, she answers for it like anyone else would.
And neither of them gets a pass because they don't have an office in the West Wing. That's the entire point. You don't need an official government title to benefit from proximity to power.
* * *

* * *
Melania has her documentary. Barron has crypto. If money is flowing to members of the president's immediate family while he controls the United States government, I want to know who's paying it, what access they have, and what they might be getting in return.
And then there are Don Jr. and Eric. Their business interests don't exist in some alternate universe disconnected from their father.

Don Jr.'s venture capital firm took a stake in Vulcan Elements. Roughly three months later, the Pentagon announced a $620 million loan to the company. That doesn't prove a crime. It does mean Congress should be crawling all over it.

Same with Ivanka. Same with Jared Kushner. If Jared is raising billions of dollars from Middle Eastern governments while simultaneously operating in the orbit of American foreign policy, "technically he's a private citizen" doesn't end the conversation.

That's where the conversation starts.
Because this is bigger than one family. We are living through a period of American history where an entire class of people faces essentially zero accountability, and that is not a partisan problem. There are Democrats in the Epstein files who have never been held accountable. There are Republicans in the Epstein files who have never been held accountable. Wall Street was never truly held accountable for 2008, and I'd argue a huge share of the rage tearing this country apart traces straight back to that failure. That isn't left or right. That's American.
And here's what's about to happen.
They're going to scurry away like rats. An unprecedented number of staff are already sprinting for the exits of this administration. They're leaving because they're betting that nobody writes down their names. They're betting nobody will remember how they used their positions to get close to powerful people, to land the next cushy gig, to cash in on the way out the door.
They're betting we forget.
I haven't forgotten. I want to know what the hell happened with Tom Homan and that $50,000 bribe. I want to know about Eric Trump trying to get confidential information to rig UFC matches in front of the White House. Hell, I'm still mad about Brett Kavanaugh's near two hundred thousand dollars of credit card debt. We were told it was for multiple packages of Washington Nationals season tickets and that his 'handful of friends' had paid him back, and then it just vanished. Who paid it off? I still want an answer to that too.
These stories don't get to evaporate because the news cycle moved on.
If there is no gravity in Washington, no accountability for anybody, from the President of the United States, to his wife, to his kids, to members of Congress, to his cabinet, Democrat or Republican, then we don't really have a country anymore. We have a banana republic. And banana-republic corruption doesn't fix itself. It has to be rooted out, root and stem.
I don't care about the pardons. I don't care about the excuses. I don't care how old anyone is or how sympathetic they look on camera. I care about one thing: proving to the American people that a functioning democracy and a functioning justice system still hold powerful people accountable for the damage they've done, the money they've stolen, and the lives they've ruined.
Because the next time a group of people thinks they can loot this country and abuse the power we entrusted to them, they should stop and think twice. They should remember exactly what happened to the last group that tried it.
That only happens if we keep the receipts and act on them.
With urgency,
--Mike

I haven't forgotten. I want to know what the hell happened with Tom Homan and that $50,000 bribe. I want to know about Eric Trump trying to get confidential information to rig UFC matches in front of the White House. Hell, I'm still mad about Brett Kavanaugh's near two hundred thousand dollars of credit card debt. We were told it was for multiple packages of Washington Nationals season tickets and that his 'handful of friends' had paid him back, and then it just vanished. Who paid it off? I still want an answer to that too. These stories don't get to evaporate because the news cycle moved on. If there is no gravity in Washington, no accountability for anybody, from the President of the United States, to his wife, to his kids, to members of Congress, to his cabinet, Democrat or Republican, then we don't really have a country anymore. We have a banana republic. And banana-republic corruption doesn't fix itself. It has to be rooted out, root and stem. I don't care about the pardons. I don't care about the excuses. I don't care how old anyone is or how sympathetic they look on camera. I care about one thing: proving to the American people that a functioning democracy and a functioning justice system still hold powerful people accountable for the damage they've done, the money they've stolen, and the lives they've ruined. Because the next time a group of people thinks they can loot this country and abuse the power we entrusted to them, they should stop and think twice. They should remember exactly what happened to the last group that tried it. That only happens if we keep the receipts and act on them. clean_body: | Fellow Conservative, I'm going to make a prediction... When the votes are counted this November, the radical left is going to be in a state of total shock. And the political establishment is going to spend weeks trying to explain what hit them. But that only happens if Republicans like you are on record before the Midterms. That is how consequential this moment is. But here is the part the pundits won't tell you. None of that happens automatically. The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports. You name it, they are on the wrong side of it. And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. I will not let that happen. And I don't think you will either. I made you a prediction at the beginning of this email. I stand by every word of it. But that prediction is built on one assumption -- that Republicans like you are engaged and ready to fight. That is where your assessment comes in. I immigrated to the United States with my family from Mexico. My dad drove buses. Today, I have the honor of representing Southeastern Arizona in Congress. Only in America is a story like mine - and YOURS - possible. And I am fighting to make sure every family in AZ-06 has that same opportunity. Here are the facts about my record and what we have delivered together– ✅ No tax on tips and overtime ✅ Social Security tax relief for seniors ✅ More than $61 million for all five counties in AZ-06 ✅ A new mission at Fort Huachuca which is expected to generate $3 billion in regional economic impact ✅ Stronger care and benefits for veterans ✅ Millions for local law enforcement and emergency services ✅ Action to ban members of Congress from trading individual stocks Independent groups have ranked me Arizona’s most effective, collaborative, and bipartisan member of Congress. That is because I work with anyone who is serious about delivering results. I don’t work for Washington. I am not a rubber stamp for anyone. I work for YOU. # [Chick-fil-A keeps humans at the drive-thru as rivals go AI](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Chick-fil-A CEO Andrew Cathy said the chain[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/79108bfc-0173-45cf-9f5c-e6b0e5a04326?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[will not let AI take drive-thru orders,](https://substack.com/redirect/79108bfc-0173-45cf-9f5c-e6b0e5a04326?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/79108bfc-0173-45cf-9f5c-e6b0e5a04326?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)even as McDonald's prepares to test voice ordering and Wendy's rolls out Google Cloud's FreshAi.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Human hospitality:** Cathy told CNBC the drive-thru should stay "human to human," adding, "We're not going to substitute that interaction with technology," because that hospitality creates a warm environment.
* **Rivals testing:** McDonald's plans to test Archy voice ordering in English and Spanish. Wendy's is deploying FreshAi, built with Google Cloud, to improve speed, accuracy and consistency.
* **Behind the counter:** Chick-fil-A is still exploring AI away from the speaker. A 2024 Georgia site uses four lanes and a conveyor that can deliver a meal to staff every six seconds.
* **Scale of the call:** The private chain posted about $23.9 billion in U.S. systemwide sales in 2025. Cathy said drive-thru orders stay with employees even as the company tests other ways to serve guests.

# [Bolsonaro's 47.1% election shock sends Brazil stocks soaring](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Right-wing senator **[Flavio Bolsonaro took 47.1% in Brazil's first round](https://substack.com/redirect/0e4e839e-ee16-4782-a639-f8318be4dd37?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's 45.1%, a shock that sent MercadoLibre, Embraer, XP and the EWZ ETF higher.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Vote map:** He beat a poll-of-polls by more than 4 points, leading in Sao Paulo 51.9% to 38.2%, Minas Gerais 48.3% to 43.2%, and Rio 53.0% to 39.4%.
* **Versus 2022:** Flavio Bolsonaro topped his father Jair Bolsonaro's 2022 first-round baseline, while Lula ran behind his own prior first-round result, Market Ear said.
* **Stock tape:** **[MercadoLibre, Embraer and XP jumped](https://substack.com/redirect/06b875c8-e447-49cd-8f4e-9a3671aa5f65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , and the[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/a5f27ba7-75aa-44bb-9bc9-9870359884c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[iShares MSCI Brazil ETF](https://substack.com/redirect/a5f27ba7-75aa-44bb-9bc9-9870359884c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** rose overnight to its highest since February 2020. Conservative gains in Congress added fuel.
* **Barron 's read:** Barron's called the senator's first-round finish an upset of Lula and said several U.S.-listed Brazilian names rallied Monday on the showing.

# [Spain's left gambles the government on a Nov. 29 vote](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez **[called a Nov. 29 snap election](https://substack.com/redirect/7f37c2a2-3f2c-469e-9dad-d9383b62cb43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Monday after parliament killed his emergency housing package, betting rent anger **[can save a Socialist government that trails in the polls.](https://substack.com/redirect/c21ce92e-0c6b-4e4a-9d9e-27078266e40e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Housing package failed:** Rejected measures would have paused evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, raised taxes on tourist apartments, extended pre-2028 leases by two years, and limited investment-firm home buys.
* **Street and China:** Protests followed September's eviction of an 87-year-old disabled woman from a home of 70 years. Consello said a right government could drop Spain's softer China line and reopen NATO spending.
* **Polls and odds:** A 40dB poll had opponents PP at 31.6%, PSOE at 27.4% and Vox at 18.4%. Eurasia sees a 70% chance of a center-right majority. Sanchez has not passed a budget in more than three years.
* **Bond market shrug:** **[Spain's 10-year was little changed at 4.08%](https://substack.com/redirect/4b3fef48-6713-4e41-bf25-ff726568e61e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**, and the spread widened 3 basis points to 65. Goldman said the ECB bar is lower for an "innocent bystander" like Spain than for France.

# [Goldman co-CEO: cut spending or yields keep climbing](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Goldman Sachs International co-CEO Anthony Gutman **[said Monday](https://substack.com/redirect/f07ce669-4e34-4fd7-b101-8a9941825d21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that lower deficits and more durable growth are[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/24d01c5d-68a9-4169-b1c5-43e12e83cbb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[the only lasting answer](https://substack.com/redirect/24d01c5d-68a9-4169-b1c5-43e12e83cbb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to a Western bond rout now centered on France.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **London warning:** Gutman told CNBC "we need lower fiscal deficits, and we need more durable economic growth," naming energy costs and the labor market as the drivers markets are watching.
* **Yield tape:** The U.S. 10-year was last at 5.2581%. **[France's](https://substack.com/redirect/70d7102d-a5d5-45ab-b90f-4de2c999b73d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** 10-year stood at 4.8812%, a Friday high since 2002, with debt at 119% of GDP and a 340 billion euro 2027 borrow planned.
* **Not a crisis yet:** TD said "a fiscal apocalypse is not upon us just yet," seeing interest near $1.1 trillion this year. BMO said the rise has "largely been a real rates story."
* **Euro and spread:** The **[Euro touched $1.1160, weakest since May 2025,](https://substack.com/redirect/9886a7ac-b10e-4a69-b21c-f01b9c914113?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** then sat at $1.1176. The OAT-Bund spread ended the week at 140 basis points, a 34 point gain and the largest in 17 years.

# [NYC puts four AI labs under oath as Musk is subpoenaed](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Senior staff[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/8b09e0f1-07be-4d20-a90d-e08788b747e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta testify under oath at 11 a.m.](https://substack.com/redirect/8b09e0f1-07be-4d20-a90d-e08788b747e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/8b09e0f1-07be-4d20-a90d-e08788b747e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)ET Monday before all 51 New York City Council members, alongside researchers who quit the labs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/22214ddf-07c1-414a-9b5d-91e2756328ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Who is sworn:** Witnesses include Logan Graham, Morgan Dwyer, Alice Friend and Shane Cahill, plus former researchers Jacob Coxon, Alex Turner and Daniel Kokotajlo.
* **Subpoena threat:** NYC Council Speaker Julie Menin said firms "owe it to the public" to answer under oath. Coxon has said the labs are "gambling with our lives." Three companies agreed only after a subpoena threat.
* **SpaceX no-show:** The Council subpoenaed Elon Musk or another SpaceXAI representative. Menin said the city may seek New York State Supreme Court enforcement if the unit does not comply.

| | | **We are less than 29 days from Election Day, and South Central Texas cannot afford to send another Trump-backed yes-man to Congress. ** I was born and raised on the West Side of San Antonio by a hard-working mom who taught me what it means to work hard. And with Washington politicians like Bryan Steil disconnected from reality, folks really appreciate that kind of honesty. Folks, it's easy to be cynical about politics these days. But candidates like Mitchell, who are everyday people ready to take on corporate MAGA yes-men like Bryan Steil, give me hope. If you agree, we need your help. If you have saved your information with ActBlue Express, your donation will process instantly. | | | **** | ** | | ** | ** | | ** | ** With care, Brett Mitchell Berman's Campaign Manager | | | | Mitchell is a devoted husband, father of two girls, and Packers season ticket holder who still believes in the promise of the American Dream—even as that dream becomes harder to reach for so many. With more than 23 years of experience in healthcare, Mitchell is a registered nurse who has spent over a decade serving veterans, active duty servicemembers, and their families at the VA. He never thought he’d run for office, but he’s running for Congress because he’s sick of the corrupt career politicians in Washington who are enriching themselves and their big donors at the expense of regular people, and he believes we deserve a system that puts our health and well-being first, not corporate profits. Mitchell is challenging the Republican incumbent Bryan Steil, a career politician and former corporate lawyer, and he needs you on his team to win. Prefer to donate via mail? _**The weak department?**_ I enlisted in the Marine Corps right out of high school. I made sergeant, then spent decades in the Army and retired as a Brigadier General. After 9/11, I led infantry soldiers in combat in Afghanistan. In 2014, I took a team into Liberia while Ebola was killing thousands, because that was the mission and somebody had to go. **I never served with a single weak person in 40 years.** Not the young soldiers who walked patrols knowing what could be waiting for them. Not the medics, mechanics, and cooks who kept us alive and moving. Not the military families who held everything together at home while we were gone. So who does Pete Hegseth think he is? **Our armed forces have never been weak. Not under any president or any party. Those men and women were strong long before he got a podium, and they'll be strong long after he's gone.** Northwest Georgia is full of veterans and military families who know that truth. They deserve a representative who will stand up and say it proudly. Right now, Clay Fuller holds this seat, and I haven't heard him say a word. On November 3, I'm asking voters to send someone to Congress who knows what our troops are made of, because I served with them. **We have 29 days left. Every dollar helps us get this message on TV screens, in mailboxes, and on veterans' doors across the district before Election Day. So I am asking: Can you chip in $25 right now to send a veteran to Congress who will stand up to Pete Hegseth?**

[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Hi there,

Our first debate is tomorrow, and we could really use your
help.
[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/20149?amount=25&t=1001&akid=1952%2E181023%2EgVftrT ]Will you step up today

want your governor fighting for?

To drive down costs. From the grocery store to the gas pump, from the

Friend,
Early voting is almost here and I want to give you a direct update from the ground.
Starting now, Turning Point PAC will be shifting into higher and higher gears every week as we fund the immediate surge of ballot-chasers across America.
This week: **Arizona. Nevada. Michigan. Pennsylvania. Ohio. Indiana. Wisconsin. New Hampshire.**
We've been on calls with our teams in every one of these states this week. The energy is there. More chasers are being recruited, and trained. The infrastructure we've been building since January is ready.
[What we need now is the resources to run it at full speed](https://links.conservative-usa.com/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=479f8d31be0c4f7987d85472506115f5&_e=BfvplCOX6iP-BTYXnxH0_G_yKZZFT8tftkR97WVFS06TANRF-0zhZgI6FCtO6MdtPp9Hk1wOLR-G-63cwhFAbwZ5A9sddjPwPc2X0V7OGqXeQ8uPIOH1cfOrcz5QEywAs2-S8YUSPNLvxe7Dj8ua3Ws7WGPDyxGcQQjGJPjBicS130gDmduT5HaeQkPu72AMPa4MuDlRKS7D4BFLugOKkRUQqLB46ni3LSgYxSheBCUh9L9ejgkioyy5x2_SNagi2chXArd6botU_yEt-WWtYgjsK8mZtdAjh2ABII5eowtOv2Jsngf5OFGRf8uzvNRd75XV5xGvSBz1aNGoX3sZ9NRgN6PXS3vkG0HlZOt4xjNjulpKxGk7clVyI9wSinmg8koyX-13rV_owbjTauRJKtVREXHpJuDG2WZiy9J0kvrTlMGqJXeDGxXvk0Cu1JaG) — because early voting begins in fewer than **eight weeks** and there is no recovery window if we come up short.

[BACK THE SURGE](https://links.conservative-usa.com/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=479f8d31be0c4f7987d85472506115f5&_e=BfvplCOX6iP-BTYXnxH0_G_yKZZFT8tftkR97WVFS06TANRF-0zhZgI6FCtO6MdtPp9Hk1wOLR-G-63cwhFAbwZ5A9sddjPwPc2X0V7OGqXYIem74itxJ15N8WimCWFHlm8DI8Qsh2m7VtvDUyZcbNxTS1LFCtz_SSV7oMdLZL_X0Ips8bnJIIIUEr4dxYpTWcNykaOVvVPsMNPMvMnTgNUhtkrmlXm4CzDm3xyxCOnKviUOEgWeWnxuZg7Bq30fchwX0IsOKfLEMYXWxp2vC0dnv2g_nK-U8k1BGJaCasYGv_lBFd53svJYpIMvtV_7v9VTFef_ww9Mb0CfXYCQJfgLUqAQaemo7_oMVD8dz5b5d70nqMkkNsXEE8_UEgVVoSuyXDMDItbVIc0DlWq5_43Ehv4c0mtmJjPfTZPWGIGpZVGonIe20E1b92t5MulD)

Let me be direct about what this moment means.
Midterm races are decided by turnout margins that would look like rounding errors in a presidential race. A few thousand votes in a handful of swing districts in Michigan or Pennsylvania or Nevada — that's the difference between keeping the House and handing Hakeem Jeffries and his communist caucus the gavel!
Our ballot-chasers are in those districts **right now.**
But a ground operation at this scale — eight states, hundreds of chasers, sustained through eight weeks of early voting — costs real money. Every day we're underfunded is a day we're leaving doors unknocked and ballots uncollected in districts we cannot afford to lose.
I've never asked more urgently than I'm asking right now. [**Will you back the surge?**](https://links.conservative-usa.com/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=479f8d31be0c4f7987d85472506115f5&_e=BfvplCOX6iP-BTYXnxH0_G_yKZZFT8tftkR97WVFS06TANRF-0zhZgI6FCtO6MdtPp9Hk1wOLR-G-63cwhFAbwZ5A9sddjPwPc2X0V7OGqXtuuFcADwFoYrhlsrF8KZK898oX7Mi5IyYpTOG5nvoUJAciXBuB7DSCqcMXuC2yNQ0S8Lvg9a5-GyyfTzvRZKU8hFASeT6CcAGb8L3tRDx1AcAFZduvgWCUIJZqLVs5yIBifnwzKFMbUQsDU5GJCiZi9w-F7J7vQBuup1XCBMglIZn9aGv2g18toazKottKnszHanScvovr2744oWwQjvDpvPSLW2xE9bvK7V1Srw4LrBkhzv9XhCEm5bRxmC3T89M_5_7D5KUU2LUw5xshR7EZn0-WRhEUrG9LLdm5WscEqdOqnnen2hLmjUCs7lP0TObSkXhAbcY9nkH04-vlaE8)

Eight states. Eight weeks. Everything we've built comes down to this.

For America,

Tyler Bowyer
Executive Director

Peter,
_**For 45 days, a 12-year-old girl lived through a nightmare no child should ever experience.** _ She had been trafficked, drugged, abused, and held against her will in a homeless encampment in California. **For 45 days, it seemed as if everyone had forsaken her.** **For 45 days, she suffered a living hell.** **For 45 days, she endured untold horrors.** [ _**Then came Day 46. That was the day our team at Heroes for Humanity went in and brought her out.** _ ](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=69a7de60fee744aaa42ccb6206206873&_e=QTTEaAPWUXZfkUQYsYb8NI4KG4BANcciuduIqyviizYj4Q1aYU-08H3duIiTKEawBYdEwH82EfdljlnyuTUK4Ac6h02h5GoWlcX8sZFvOOAKO1baIAasaF9LNUbwG7f7Zo1jyXeLR0wHwzQM09wrIDvnoK6zAY-JXPAky8XHjkEwuJziC5dVAkE7ySgD_qHdjQeQEUbKVl_wZ9ZLXYlYq2YJIRF_Gp34hWEERBrPYKo5SyDfnsQrFQ1-4NreASbwSLAbaeE6XqZiQZHXIaWrHztA1_OzZatCtMxlPRIH81ticwqw0Yzu5AppMgmZFJ7DUVlSlxis3JouP2HnkNmabyN2czab7kdSaUI-t5DiTQ2jYjWZvAQbSO4fZz1W5w1NH6_ZZAcsOeDLrSQWdf6GpKF1VkI9AX5K5AYenY8XklnbFZLKlb0TKIT-HXvETbP7qGTKK8PKNf19GMr9Vv55e_qjy03zeE0q9OirLjvQOg2V6xMclt6w_reD9oLd1Gb6kA-aWIqUN5RvBnZKZzyhe0hE_l47H1sZ5_MsdPLLWFIvXOF5BFfaYiBRlk0Z6kvqR-VZuxTkevNITvaS9znKU4osY0GFuSyQRgPJdT0Pa5cQzqlopo5mAj49cA_INJ2Sj_hRi0sVaX09Yl9kay6tuFZo93ELoLUgd6LoaXA9ECd1W0zguPVYSXw-e_gP7G7kR--y-tbPVffX3ZuLdNg_7mrdisCq7py1LoRTtYJCoGI%3D)
My name is Dennis Price, and I want to tell you why I'm sharing her story with you today. I believe God puts people in our path for a reason. Sometimes He calls us to pray. Sometimes He calls us to give. And sometimes He puts someone in front of us who desperately needs help, and then the Lord asks, “Who will go?” I have spent more than 19 years across various special operations units and private military contracting, and now I serve as a humanitarian and evangelist. I've seen suffering most people thankfully never will. I started Heroes for Humanity during the collapse in Afghanistan, watching Americans and vetted Afghan allies get hunted while the systems built to get them out failed completely. A small team and I helped rescue dozens of them. **That crucible proved how powerful it can be when good people refuse to look the other way.** We’ve carried that mission to all corners of the world, including responding to devastating earthquakes in Venezuela and Colombia this summer and the deadly Texas Hill Country floods last year. Our team is made up of veteran special operators, first responders, medical professionals, and everyday heroes who are willing to go into the places others can’t – or won’t – to rescue people in desperate need. [ _**For that little girl, it meant getting her out of an unimaginable situation and bringing her home.** _ ](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=69a7de60fee744aaa42ccb6206206873&_e=QTTEaAPWUXZfkUQYsYb8NI4KG4BANcciuduIqyviizYj4Q1aYU-08H3duIiTKEawBYdEwH82EfdljlnyuTUK4Ac6h02h5GoWlcX8sZFvOOAKO1baIAasaF9LNUbwG7f7Zo1jyXeLR0wHwzQM09wrIDvnoK6zAY-JXPAky8XHjkEwuJziC5dVAkE7ySgD_qHdjQeQEUbKVl_wZ9ZLXYlYq2YJIRF_Gp34hWEERBrPYKo5SyDfnsQrFQ1-4NreASbwS933r5PozwDags2ladkW1hF7uyGNyTXgoTM6fo7k-P3n6da_hbAWGV6-SNdbbTKm5MqivXePqRzCJ5VT7g8YKMXPyXo-TS--B_lyWCZAF3dJd6i9MtIVnAcrzwfnqLcZs61AlMmV5DnYwcVLrf3HC1ixQIcRkKzQddx1EDlAF0LsatIwF-HSD1KgpXeDzbmXJUB8AUqIEDMfKwsZze4P9AokBk1MF4Dqblmt4KxSCHvAIAxzIhDyZ0plrULVAprFPpUJt6qvwtb_kkhOGkz8fKtPzW-TrYcewvjWciBf2chjHa4Zpnl_mMaSnb7BNtrAxW_JlFS-6ado-Wdz1hr90a8bAMEJQGOLg25vwQB81feSgVXSWNxuRV2gU0w_u6ZGrcO1yk57R5OWq80lvmVfq4tU_igkjguK0672M1ETPgqXDnCCqWF-s-uOf3zNwNP6C8gtjpvn0HEuV0ucRazopJ4twf81jOU94Bl71oMm9ks%3D) In other cases, it could mean delivering lifesaving aid after a natural disaster, pulling families from a warzone, or simply being there on the worst day of someone’s life and reminding them that they have not been forgotten. But we can't wait until the next desperate call comes to get ready. Our operators have to be trained. Our equipment has to be ready. Vehicles need fuel. Medical supplies need to be stocked. clean_body: For 45 days, she was alone and abandoned. | | | | | Peter, For 45 days, a 12-year-old girl lived through a nightmare no child should ever experience. She had been trafficked, drugged, abused, and held against her will in a homeless encampment in California. For 45 days, it seemed as if everyone had forsaken her. For 45 days, she suffered a living hell. For 45 days, she endured untold horrors. My name is Dennis Price, and I want to tell you why I'm sharing her story with you today. I believe God puts people in our path for a reason. Sometimes He calls us to pray. Sometimes He calls us to give. And sometimes He puts someone in front of us who desperately needs help, and then the Lord asks, “Who will go?” I have spent more than 19 years across various special operations units and private military contracting, and now I serve as a humanitarian and evangelist. I've seen suffering most people thankfully never will. I started Heroes for Humanity during the collapse in Afghanistan, watching Americans and vetted Afghan allies get hunted while the systems built to get them out failed completely. A small team and I helped rescue dozens of them. That crucible proved how powerful it can be when good people refuse to look the other way. We’ve carried that mission to all corners of the world, including responding to devastating earthquakes in Venezuela and Colombia this summer and the deadly Texas Hill Country floods last year. Our team is made up of veteran special operators, first responders, medical professionals, and everyday heroes who are willing to go into the places others can’t – or won’t – to rescue people in desperate need. In other cases, it could mean delivering lifesaving aid after a natural disaster, pulling families from a warzone, or simply being there on the worst day of someone’s life and reminding them that they have not been forgotten. But we can't wait until the next desperate call comes to get ready. Our operators have to be trained. Our equipment has to be ready. Vehicles need fuel. Medical supplies need to be stocked. Case File No DRT-ED-QUANTUM · Special File · Q-Day
Washington Just Put a Date on Q-Day. The Banks Started Preparing Years Ago.
A $2 billion bet on nine quantum companies, two executive orders and a hard 2030 deadline for encryption that can survive quantum attacks. The smart money moved first. Here’s the timeline, and what it says about who gets paid next.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Every bank account, card payment and wire transfer on earth is protected by encryption that today’s computers would need thousands of years to break. A large enough quantum computer could, in theory, break it in hours. Security experts call that moment “Q-Day.” This year, Washington put a date on the calendar to get ready for it, and the money started moving before most investors noticed.
The timeline
| | Who Moved First
---|---
| | EARLY
---
The banks
Over the last several years, giants like JPMorgan and HSBC built dedicated quantum research teams, hiring physicists and testing quantum-safe encryption on their own systems.
| | MAY 2026
---
Washington’s checkbook
The administration committed $2 billion to nine quantum computing companies, including equity stakes. Quantum stocks jumped on the first reports, before the details were official.
| | JUNE 22, 2026
---
The executive orders
Trump signed two orders: one to accelerate quantum computing, one to defend against quantum-enabled code-breaking.
| | NOW
---
The deadlines
Federal contractors must meet NIST’s post-quantum standards by December 31, 2030. Agencies must move their most critical systems by the end of 2031.
The evidence board
| | What the Orders Actually Do
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the defense order.** “Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks” requires every agency to name a post-quantum migration lead within 30 days, and requires federal contractors to adopt NIST’s post-quantum standards by 2030.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the build order.** “Ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation” launches an effort to build a large-scale quantum computer at a Department of Energy facility, and points to “advance market commitments,” meaning government promises to buy.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the market’s verdict.** The day after the orders, Quantinuum rose 13%, Infleqtion 12% and IBM 5%, while the Nasdaq fell 2.2%.
Decoder
| | The Date That Changes Everything
---|---
| | “Federal contractors must comply with NIST’s post-quantum standards by 2030.”— Executive order on quantum security, June 2026
---|---
What it says
Government suppliers need new encryption within about four years.
What it means
**Our theory:** a deadline turns a research topic into a purchasing requirement. Thousands of contractors, banks and agencies now have to buy quantum-related hardware, software and expertise on a fixed schedule. When the government sets a deadline and writes checks at the same time, the companies supplying the scarce pieces don’t have to wait for the market to believe them.
Still blacked out
| | What the Timeline Doesn’t Show
---|---
| ██ REDACTED ██
---
Exactly when a quantum computer will be able to break today’s encryption. Estimates range from years to over a decade, and nobody wants to be late.
| ██ REDACTED ██
---
Which of the nine companies backed in May will get the bulk of future government contracts.
| ██ REDACTED ██
---
How much banks are actually spending on quantum defense. They don’t break it out, and they don’t like to talk about it.
| ClassificationTransition
---
Quantum just moved from science project to government deadline. The banks prepared early, Washington wrote the checks, and the orders set the clock. The question now isn’t whether the spending comes. It’s who supplies the hardware everyone suddenly needs.
| The riddle · answer at the end of the fileBanks can hire every cryptographer in the world. What’s the one thing their money can’t produce on its own?
---
|
---
Riddle answer
**The physical machine.** Banks can write software and rewrite their encryption. But quantum hardware takes specialized chips, extreme cooling and years of engineering that only a handful of companies can deliver. **Our theory:** when everyone faces the same deadline, the scarce part of the supply chain gets paid first.

With a classified leak... a burst of unusual activity on Wall Street... and one small clue buried in the timeline. Individually, none of it proves much. Put together, though, it raises an uncomfortable question: | | (ad by Behind the Markets) | | | | Case File No DRT-ED-QUANTUM · Special File · Q-Day Washington Just Put a Date on Q-Day. The Banks Started Preparing Years Ago. A $2 billion bet on nine quantum companies, two executive orders and a hard 2030 deadline for encryption that can survive quantum attacks. The smart money moved first. Here’s the timeline, and what it says about who gets paid next. Threat level 4/5 — Elevated | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|--- | Every bank account, card payment and wire transfer on earth is protected by encryption that today’s computers would need thousands of years to break. A large enough quantum computer could, in theory, break it in hours. Security experts call that moment “Q-Day.” This year, Washington put a date on the calendar to get ready for it, and the money started moving before most investors noticed. The timeline | | Who Moved First ---|--- | | EARLY The banks Over the last several years, giants like JPMorgan and HSBC built dedicated quantum research teams, hiring physicists and testing quantum-safe encryption on their own systems. | | MAY 2026 Washington’s checkbook The administration committed $2 billion to nine quantum computing companies, including equity stakes. Quantum stocks jumped on the first reports, before the details were official. | | JUNE 22, 2026 The executive orders Trump signed two orders: one to accelerate quantum computing, one to defend against quantum-enabled code-breaking. | | NOW The deadlines Federal contractors must meet NIST’s post-quantum standards by December 31, 2030. Agencies must move their most critical systems by the end of 2031. The evidence board | | What the Orders Actually Do ---|--- | EVIDENCE Exhibit A — the defense order. “Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks” requires every agency to name a post-quantum migration lead within 30 days, and requires federal contractors to adopt NIST’s post-quantum standards by 2030. | EVIDENCE Exhibit B — the build order. “Ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation” launches an effort to build a large-scale quantum computer at a Department of Energy facility, and points to “advance market commitments,” meaning government promises to buy. | EVIDENCE Exhibit C — the market’s verdict. The day after the orders, Quantinuum rose 13%, Infleqtion 12% and IBM 5%, while the Nasdaq fell 2.2%. Decoder | | The Date That Changes Everything ---|--- | | “Federal contractors must comply with NIST’s post-quantum standards by 2030.”— Executive order on quantum security, June 2026 ---|--- What it says Government suppliers need new encryption within about four years. What it means Our theory: a deadline turns a research topic into a purchasing requirement. Thousands of contractors, banks and agencies now have to buy quantum-related hardware, software and expertise on a fixed schedule. When the government sets a deadline and writes checks at the same time, the companies supplying the scarce pieces don’t have to wait for the market to believe them. Still blacked out | | What the Timeline Doesn’t Show ---|--- | ██ REDACTED ██ Exactly when a quantum computer will be able to break today’s encryption. Estimates range from years to over a decade, and nobody wants to be late. | ██ REDACTED ██ Which of the nine companies backed in May will get the bulk of future government contracts. | ██ REDACTED ██ How much banks are actually spending on quantum defense. They don’t break it out, and they don’t like to talk about it. | ClassificationTransition Quantum just moved from science project to government deadline. The banks prepared early, Washington wrote the checks, and the orders set the clock. The question now isn’t whether the spending comes. It’s who supplies the hardware everyone suddenly needs. | The riddle · answer at the end of the fileBanks can hire every cryptographer in the world. What’s the one thing their money can’t produce on its own? | Riddle answer The physical machine. Banks can write software and rewrite their encryption. But quantum hardware takes specialized chips, extreme cooling and years of engineering that only a handful of companies can deliver. Our theory: when everyone faces the same deadline, the scarce part of the supply chain gets paid first. | | (ad by Behind the Markets) | | (ad by Behind the Markets) | | | At Deep Regime Trends, we write for people who think for themselves. Inside Elections pointed out that Republican incumbent David Valadao lost this seat during Trump's first midterm, and that Democratic candidates received more votes than he did in this year's all-party primary.
Valadao's opponent, community college professor Randy Villegas, has proven this seat is winnable. Villegas overcame more than $4 million in outside spending against him to win his primary, and a public poll of the general election shows him leading Valadao 48-44.
Mail-in ballots start arriving Monday, and forecasters have flagged that this hard-to-poll region will likely see low turnout.
